items.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Financial Foundation Models: A Survey
items.summary: Financial foundation models increasingly support workflows spanning financial question answering, disclosure analysis, forecasting, and decision-making. In these settings, uncertainty may concern whether evidence is valid and available at the relevant time, whether an interpretation is justified, which outcomes remain plausible, or which action is preferred under costs and risk constraints. Because these objects arise at different points in a workflow, uncertainty cannot be reduced to confidence in a final output. We introduce a source-aware framework that distinguishes six sources of uncertainty across evidence and context, model and inference, and outcome and action, while treating…

items.title: RobPiCFM: A Training-Free Target-Conditioned Method with Foundation Models for Robotic Picking in Clutter
items.summary: Picking objects from clutter remains a challenging problem in robotic manipulation, as it requires connecting object-level perception, grasp generation, collision-aware selection, and robot motion execution in unstructured scenes. In this paper, we present RobPiCFM, an open-source, trainingfree method for target-conditioned picking in cluttered scenes. The proposed method combines pretrained foundation-modelbased perception with RGB-D geometry, 6D object pose estimation and tracking, grasp candidate generation, constraintbased grasp filtering, and motion planning. Unlike end-toend manipulation policies, the method does not require taskspecific policy learning and relies instead on…

items.title: Adversarial Post-Training of Foundation Models for High-Frequency Trading
items.summary: While autoregressive foundation models trained on limit order book (LOB) data show state-of-the-art performance for market simulation, pre-training with cross-entropy neither penalizes the compounding of sampling errors over free-running rollouts nor targets desired market properties. We introduce a post-training method for LOB foundation models using a Wasserstein generative adversarial network (GAN) objective. A critic, trained online on rollouts through the true, non-differentiable matching engine, guides updates from evolution strategies over rank-4 LoRA perturbations of the pre-trained generator, under a KL trust region. For efficiency, we use EGGROLL (Evolution Guided GeneRal…

items.title: Organelle distribution and protein translation defects in radial glia cells with mutations in Eml1
items.summary: Abstract Cerebral cortical development is a finely regulated process, depending on key neuronal progenitors, giving rise to post-mitotic neurons that migrate to superficial regions in the developing brain. Disruptions can give rise to severe cortical malformations that are associated with intellectual disability and intractable epilepsy. Mutations in EML1/Eml1 , coding for a microtubule (MT)-associated protein, lead to subcortical heterotopia (SH) in both humans and mice. In developing mutant mouse brains, ectopic apical radial glia (aRG) progenitors were found outside the normal proliferative ventricular zone (VZ). The normal role of Eml1 in these cells remains to be precisely determined.…

items.title: Evolved Spiking Neural Networks for EEG Seizure Detection: Calcium Dynamics and Delay Mechanics
items.summary: arXiv:2611.03841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neuroevolution can discover compact network designs that are hard to specify by hand. The EONS framework evolves the topology, weights, thresholds and delays of neuromorphic spiking networks without gradients. We tested whether giving integrate-and-fire (IF) neurons an activity-dependent calcium current (Ca-IF neurons) improves evolved networks for EEG seizure detection, with calcium parameters fixed, shared across a network, or evolved for each neuron. On 10 held-out CHB-MIT patients never seen in training, per-neuron calcium raised the record-level Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) from 0.592 to 0.726 over 20 independent runs (p =…

items.title: Prototypes of the Mind: A Unified Framework for Probing the Visual Brain
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning has driven substantial progress in modeling fMRI responses, yet most existing approaches are optimized for a single objective---such as neural encoding, stimulus decoding, or post hoc interpretation---making it difficult to obtain a coherent account of neural representations. We introduce a unified framework that connects vision foundation models to brain activity while supporting neural analysis from multiple complementary perspectives. Our approach replaces black-box features with a sparse, interpretable representation composed of visual prototypes, and links these prototypes to voxel responses through a linear readout. This…

items.title: Pyramidal Columns Acting as Attention Heads
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can the functional architecture of a Transformer attention head be given a biological construction? More specifically, could a suitable group of pyramidal columns in posterior temporal language regions (PTLRs) constitute the biological construction of a neuromorphic mechanical realization of an attention head, under a mathematical instantiation that need not coincide with its standard Transformer instantiation? This paper investigates this hypothesis by examining possible correspondences between the functional organization of attention heads and neurophysiological mechanisms operating within and across pyramidal columns involved in human…

items.title: DeNA-SGN: Deterministic Neighborhood Aggregation for Verified Spiking Graph Inference
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph learning on neuromorphic substrates requires an explicit spiking realization of neighborhood aggregation, supporting control and classification. We propose DeNA-SGN, which combines fixed OR and tie-inclusive Majority aggregation of binary node features with a learned signed-weight threshold classifier. A degree-dependent inhibitory construction implements Majority through shared control neurons, enabling a complete circuit compilation into SuperNeuroMAT. Across seven datasets and 41 mapped classifiers, native simulation matches the exported ANN on every evaluated class decision and output-spike pattern. On the new confirmatory Amazon…

items.title: FROM MATHEMATICAL SUPERINTELLIGENCE TO PHYSICAL DISCOVERY
items.summary: Recent advances in artificial intelligence suggest that coordinated populations of capablereasoning agents may solve mathematical problems of extraordinary complexity. Suchachievements raise a distinct question: Can comparable systems advance fundamental physicsby identifying the physical mechanisms responsible for nature’s observed behavior, rather thanmerely extending mathematical descriptions already accepted by scientific convention?This paper proposes a human-directed, observation-first AI research architecture forinvestigating Space-Phase (SP3) theory. SP3 proposes that physical space is a participatingmedium interacting with energy through nested configurations, conditioning,…

items.title: SpaRRTa: A Synthetic Benchmark for Evaluating Spatial Intelligence in Visual Foundation Models
items.summary: Abstract Visual Foundation Models (VFMs), such as DINO and CLIP, excel in semantic understanding of images but exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities, which limits their applicability to embodied systems. As a result, recent work has incorporated some 3D tasks (such as depth estimation) into VFM training. However, VFM performance remains inconsistent across other spatial tasks, raising the question of whether these models truly possess spatial awareness or overfit to specific 3D objectives. To address this question, we introduce the Spatial Relation Recognition Task (SpaRRTa) benchmark, which evaluates the ability of VFMs to identify static directional relations between visible…

items.title: Laser-guided ion dynamics in a dual-mode memristor for bioinspired neuronal and synaptic integration
items.summary: Abstract Neuromorphic computing aims to replicate the parallel, adaptive nature of biological intelligence in electronic systems. Despite considerable advances in memristor technology, material-encoded neurosynaptic bifunctionality has not been demonstrated. We introduce a laser-guided dual-mode memristor that integrates both volatility for neuronal spiking and nonvolatility for synaptic plasticity within a single-phase material. By precisely modulating silver ion dynamics through XeCl excimer laser irradiation, we achieve local and dynamic control of the dual-mode memristive behavior without requiring a heterogeneous device array or stacking. The neurosynaptic tunability with optimal…

items.title: UVM: neuron verification
items.summary: The significant growth in Neuromorphic engineering in the last few years has generated a multitude of biologically plausible neuron models that have been developed into Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) and Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) designs. These neuron models range in complexity, from the Integrate and Fire model to the Hodgkin-Huxley model. When creating fixed point implementations of these models, it is prudent to ensure the dynamic range of the fixed point conversion has been correctly chosen. However, verifying neuron model implementations in simulation requires a significant amount of time to achieve an acceptable coverage; that is, everything that could be…

items.title: Learning the spikes
items.summary: Existing AI methods consume vast amounts of power due to their large scale and intrinsic redundancy. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a biologically plausible alternative that enables systems that are of a low Size, Weight and Power (SWaP) profile, once implemented. However, there is limited commercial availability of Neuromorphic processors to efficiently implement these SNNs on chip, resulting in a requirement to develop FPGA-based Neuromorphic processing. The same can be said for Neuromorphic sensors, driving a trend to develop techniques for encoding existing sensor data into an event-based format for use with Neuromorphic processors. This paper presents a very efficient, low power…

items.title: Modelling dynamic systems transfer functions from events in computational neuromorphic imaging
items.summary: Event Vision Sensing (EVS) report threshold crossings of log-irradiance, so a static optical system imaging a static scene produces no output at all. The classical procedure for measuring a Point Spread Function (PSF), illuminating the system with a constant point source, therefore has no event-based equivalent: the probe must carry a temporal profile, and that profile becomes part of the measurement. A growing body of Computational Neuromorphic Imaging (CNI) work already exploits this, pairing engineered or modulated optics with event sensing, but each system adopts a particular excitation together with a particular reading of the event stream without the correspondence between the two…

items.title: Candidate alternative splice-junction architecture at a Ganoderma carnitine acetyltransferase-like locus: an accession-traceable RNA-seq reanalysis
items.summary: Abstract A focused reanalysis of public Ganoderma transcriptomic resources evaluated two candidate splice-junction paths (A and B) at a putative carnitine acetyltransferase-like locus (MSTRG.5584). Forty RNA-seq run labels from five genomic backgrounds were reconciled with accession metadata and examined using targeted splice-spanning read counts; 11 undercovered libraries underwent complete read-1 recounting. Both candidate junction paths were observed in all five backgrounds. In libraries with any focal read support, mean junction-A fractions were descriptively greater in mycelium-labeled than in fruiting-body-labeled groups, with background-level differences ranging from +0.190 to…

items.title: Infrared Life: Coherent Josephson Radiation in Microtubule Networks, Radiometric Signatures, and Quantum Synchronization in Living Systems
items.summary: This paper investigates non-thermal electromagnetic radiation generated within livingorganisms. In addition to universal blackbody radiation dominating the infrared spectrum,living systems generate narrow-band, coherent infrared radiation aligned with the 8–13 µmtransparency window of Earth’s atmosphere. This emission avoids complete thermalization,acts independently of classical thermal radiance, and represents an evolutionary hallmarkof biological order. The radiation is shown to originate within multi-connected networks ofsuperconducting microtubules functioning as Josephson junctions during action potentialpropagation. We present radiometric measurements on porcine brain tissue slices…

items.title: GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence: Antecedents, perceived usefulness, AI ethics awareness, and career readiness outcomes.
items.summary: This study examines GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence (GAISC) among accounting and auditing students and its relationships with GenAI readiness (GAR), perceived ease of use (PEOU), digital learning self-efficacy (DLSE), facilitating conditions (FC), perceived usefulness (PU), AI ethics awareness (AIEA), and career readiness (CR). The model is anchored in Socio-Technical Systems Theory (STS) and Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), with technology readiness, TAM, self-efficacy, and facilitating-condition logic used as construct-level underpinning mechanisms. Survey data from 471 students at five Vietnamese universities were analyzed using PLS-SEM, complemented by a…

items.title: In silico drug discovery framework leveraging biomedical foundation models and evaluating generative models-a use case on 3CL pro .
items.summary: AI models such as foundation models and generative models have shown promise for aiding drug discovery alongside traditional cheminformatics and bioinformatics tools and physics-based approaches. In this study, we design a workflow that integrates these AI methods to generate molecules alongside established informatic and predictive filtering approaches to streamline downselection of molecules from the massive and noisy result sets generated by AI. This workflow evaluates generative methods based on validity, reliability, diversity, similarity, hallucination and campaign needs. Analyses are made on the original proprietary dataset to determine molecular property thresholds for screening…

items.title: MicroDUET: a dual-headed genomic foundation model for pathogen surveillance
items.summary: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa. On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head returned the correct…

items.title: Systematic benchmarking of molecular foundation models for natural-product annotation and biosynthetic inference
items.summary: Abstract Molecular foundation models offer a potential route to improve natural-product annotation and support biosynthetic inference, but their utility across these tasks remains insufficiently characterized. We benchmarked eight foundation-model representations against Morgan fingerprints across five tasks covering natural-product-likeness, natural product chemical class prediction, PMN and KEGG pathway association, and PlantCyc reaction-neighbor prediction. Models were evaluated under random and scaffold-based splits using both full data and sample-efficiency settings. In the full data setting, MolFormer achieved the highest mean AUROC for natural product likeness prediction, while…

items.title: LUNA-FM: a subword foundation model for long non-coding RNAs for functional inference.
items.summary: RNA foundation models (FMs) have shown promise for RNA identification and functional annotation. However, many use single-nucleotide tokenization, which produces long input sequences and can increase computational costs when modelling long RNAs, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). To address these limitations, we introduce LUNA-FM ( Length-efficient s U bword-based N ucleic A cid F oundation M odel) , an RNA language model pretrained on approximately 28 million redundancy-filtered ncRNA sequences. LUNA-FM combines subword tokenization with a long context transformer, enabling efficient modelling of long RNA transcripts. We systematically evaluate tokenization strategies and…

items.title: Understanding plant UPR from structural and comparative perspectives.
items.summary: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is central to protein, lipid, Ca2+, and redox homeostasis. ER stress occurs when oxidative protein-folding capacity is exceeded or lipid composition becomes abnormal. To restore ER and cellular homeostasis, the cell initiates the unfolded protein response (UPR)-a transcriptional response that amplifies the ER's capacity for protein folding, degradation, and lipid biosynthesis. Our understanding of plant UPR activation mechanisms remains limited compared with yeast and mammalian systems. Here, we compare the structural composition of the plant UPR sensors, inositol-requiring enzyme 1 and basic-region leucine zipper 28, with their yeast and animal homologs;…

items.title: Toward precision nanomedicine via artificial intelligence guided design and prediction.
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing nanomedicine development by linking formulation variables and biological context with delivery, therapeutic efficacy, and safety. This review examines AI assisted formulation design, centralized formulation databases, prediction of nanoparticle self assembly, and models of cell and tissue selective delivery, biodistribution, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent advances in predicting nanotoxicity and nanoparticle induced immune responses further emphasize the importance of incorporating safety endpoints into nanomedicine optimization. Beyond nanocarrier engineering, foundation models and multimodal analyses of single-cell and spatial data are expanding…

items.title: Fluid eMTBR-tau243 as a Biomarker of Mixed 3-Repeat and 4-Repeat Tau Pathology.
items.summary: Neurodegenerative diseases with abnormal tau protein aggregation in the brain (ie, tauopathies) can be classified by the tau isoform that accumulates: 3-repeat (3R), 4-repeat (4R), or mixed 3R/4R tauopathies, which include chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), some forms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, and Alzheimer disease (AD). The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear. To evaluate biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in a range of tauopathies.…

items.title: HDAC6 Inhibition Promotes Peripheral Nerve Development and Regeneration via Neurofilament Acetylation.
items.summary: Peripheral nerve injury remains challenging due to limited neuronal regeneration. Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) regulates microtubule dynamics, but its role in peripheral nervous system (PNS) development and repair is incompletely understood. This study investigates the expression, function, and mechanism of HDAC6 in PNS maturation and regeneration. HDAC6 was abundantly expressed in dorsal root ganglia and sciatic nerves. During postnatal development (P1-P28), HDAC6 expression progressively declined, inversely correlating with increased α-tubulin K40 and global acetylation. Pharmacological HDAC6 inhibition with Tubastatin A (Tub A) or suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid (SAHA) accelerated…

items.title: NiCl 2 affect N- and O -alkylations during alkaloid biosynthesis in Penicillium oxalicum .
items.summary: Oxaline is one fungal alkaloid possessing important citotoxicity and inhibiting tubulin polymerisation. The alkaloids in this series are differentiated by the degree of alkylation promoted by SAM-dependent methyl transferases, being oxaline the end product in the biosynthetic cascade. During our studies, it was found that the addition of NiCl2 into liquid culture of P. oxalicum affect the distribution of these alkaloids, lowering the production of oxaline and enhancing the amount of methylglandicoline A and glandicoline C, two unreported natural products. Ni(II) addition also resulted in the production of a pair of E/Z isomers of N-formyl α,β-dehydro-DOPA, found only at trace amounts in…

items.title: Dual-Mode MoS 2 /PdSe 2 /WS 2 Van Der Waals Heterostructure for Self-Powered Polarization Sensing and Neuromorphic Processing.
items.summary: Harsh maritime environments demand compact visual devices capable of self-powered photodetection, polarization sensing, and motion-trajectory extraction for onboard processing. Here, we demonstrate a bias-switchable MoS2/PdSe2/WS2 van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH) that integrates self-powered polarization-sensitive photodetection and optoelectronic synaptic functionality. At a drain-source voltage (Vds) of 0 V, built-in electric fields efficiently separate photogenerated carriers, enabling self-powered broadband detection over the 405-658 nm spectral range. The device exhibits a maximum responsivity of 1345 mA W-1, a specific detectivity of 8.89 × 1010 Jones, and rapid rise/fall times…

items.title: Ion-Access Engineering for High-Performance Vertical Organic Electrolyte-Gated Transistors.
items.summary: Organic electrolyte-gated transistors (OEGTs) are promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic systems owing to their low-voltage operation and strong ionic-electronic coupling. However, in vertical OEGTs, which offer higher current densities and faster switching, the semiconductor channel is often shielded from direct electrolyte contact, limiting ionic accessibility and resulting in inefficient gate coupling and slow switching dynamics. Here, we introduce a photolithography-free ion-access strategy for vertical OEGTs, combining femtosecond laser micropatterning with inkjet-printed solid-state electrolytes. Laser-defined pores penetrating the top electrode and semiconductor…

items.title: Molecularly Programmed Stress Dissipation Strategy for Ultrastretchable Neuromorphic Electronics.
items.summary: Intrinsically stretchable organic synaptic transistors (ISOSTs) using semiconducting polymers (SPs) hold promise for on-body signal processing by mimicking biological synaptic functions and processing temporal bio-signals directly at or near the point of data acquisition. However, conventional SPs designed primarily to increase polymer softness and mechanical compliance often lack molecular-level mechanisms for effective stress dissipation, thereby limiting device-level stretchability to below 100% and causing substantial degradation in electrical performance. Here, we demonstrate ISOSTs achieving 150% device-level stretchability through molecularly programmed stress dissipation (MPSD) of…

items.title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation
items.summary: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle…

items.title: Love numbers for the Myers-Perry geometry
items.summary: We analyze Love numbers for scalar fields in the Myers-Perry geometry in arbitrary dimensions. The tidal responses of black holes are specified by two constants which encode a potential logarithmic running and the Love number. We argue that the parameter specifying the running is not sensitive to the structure of the horizon, and we explicitly compute this parameter for Myers-Perry black holes in arbitrary dimensions by utilizing the asymptotic expansion of the wave equation. The Love numbers rely on the details of the boundary conditions at the horizon, and we compute them using several distinct approximations.

items.title: The lifting problem for Galois representations of global fields
items.summary: We prove that all mod $2$ Galois representations of a global field lift modulo $4$. In contrast, for every odd prime $p$, we exhibit examples of global Galois representations modulo $p$ that do not lift modulo $p^2$. Our methods also allow us to prove liftability of generalized quaternion groups and hence to complete the classification of liftable finite groups initiated by Khare and Merkurjev.

items.title: Inter-Nanoparticle Repulsion Effect on Self-Organization in Polymer Nanocomposites: A Langevin Dynamics Simulation Study
items.summary: Demixing through liquid-liquid phase separation is relevant to nanoparticle (NP) aggregation in polymer nanocomposites (PNCs), biomolecular compartmentalization, and liquids embedded in elastic networks. Mixing-demixing phase behavior depends on factors, such as particle size distribution, system dimen-sionality, intermolecular interactions, and relative concentrations. Here, using Langevin Dynamics simu-lations, we systematically investigate the effect of inter-nanoparticle repulsion on the self-assembly of PNCs under extreme confinement. A nanoparticle assembly, in the form of a compact droplet, is immersed in a polymer matrix of semiflexible, rod-like chains. By varying the…

items.title: SpotDiff: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Zero-Shot Change Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
items.summary: Remote sensing change detection usually relies on large collections of temporally aligned, pixel-level annotations, which limits its scalability across regions, imaging platforms and application domains. Recent zero-shot approaches reduce the need for supervision, but they often localize fine-grained changes poorly because their features are coarse or inconsistent across time. We present SpotDiff, a training-free, plug-and-play framework for zero-shot change detection built by composing complementary vision foundation models. SpotDiff uses DINOv3 for semantically robust features, AnyUp to reconstruct them at pixel resolution, and SAM 3 for text-guided region-of-interest proposals, which an…

items.title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
items.summary: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on datasets that each vary one design family in one flow domain. Such datasets cannot test the least that an aerodynamic foundation model must do: predict CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling the training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. We introduce AeroZoo, a benchmark and training corpus of 3,815 time-mean solutions to the unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) equations with a transition model, across seven geometry families, eight…

items.title: HiVE-VQA: Hierarchical Interaction via Volumetric Embedding for Video Quality Assessment
items.summary: The proliferation of user-generated video content has made accurate and robust no-reference video quality assessment (NR-VQA) a highly important challenge. Existing research increasingly relies on architecturally complex multi-branch pipelines or computationally intensive fine-tuning of single-branch backbones. In this paper, we investigate whether a single frozen video foundation model can serve as an effective NR-VQA backbone, and propose HiVE-VQA, the first framework (to our knowledge) to apply a JEPA-based video encoder to this task. HiVE-VQA extracts token grids from multiple depths of a pre-trained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder and stacks them into a hierarchical spatio-temporal volume, which a…

items.title: Library of peptides: Analysis of a complex reactive mixture with the use of statistical physics and inference
items.summary: Self-assembled mixtures enable the exploration of vast chemical diversity, yet characterizing the hundreds of coexisting species they contain remains a major challenge. Standard analytical techniques such as chromatography and spectroscopy produce overlapping signals that cannot be resolved by conventional deconvolution methods, which neglect the concentration correlations imposed by the reactive network. Here, we introduce a framework that bridges statistical physics and analytical chemistry to deconvolute complex self-assembled mixtures from partial spectral data. Inspired by Potts models of protein folding, we express the chemical potential of each compound as a function of a reduced…

items.title: Acoustically driven motion of single molecules at hBN surfaces
items.summary: Developments in single-molecule imaging and sensing techniques have enabled direct observation of biomolecular dynamics at interfaces, which has important implications for the fields of membrane biophysics, nanofluidic sensing and transport. However, integrating active surface transport, localization and control over molecule motion remains challenging, limiting further progress in the realization of single-molecule devices. Here, we introduce an integrated surface acoustic wave (SAW)-hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) platform as a contactless actuation platform for directional transport of biomolecules over hBN surfaces. hBN provides an atomically flat surface on which DNA can be confined and…

items.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to…

items.title: TuMAP: A Dual-View, Morphotype-Aware Pathomics Pipeline for Quantifying Renal Tubular Remodeling
items.summary: Quantifying disease-associated renal tubular remodeling is challenging because tubular appearances are heterogeneous. We introduce TuMAP (Tubular Morphotype-Aware Pathomics), a pipeline combining (1) dual-view foundation-model representations and provisional morphotype annotation, (2) compositional and within-morphotype pathomics, and (3) patient-level statistical inference. From 456,158 tubules in 358 PAS-stained kidney biopsy slides, TuMAP identified eight image-based morphotypes, seven of which showed stable subsampling assignments. Across 219 patients in six diagnostic groups, diabetic nephropathy (DN) and tubulointerstitial nephritis/acute tubular injury (TIN/ATI) each differed from…

items.title: Reasoning Supervision and Capability Retention in LoRA Domain Adaptation
items.summary: Fine-tuning foundation models on financial data has a wide range of applications, including identifying event types from news, monitoring risk and compliance language, and answering questions over filings and earnings calls. In this setting, the main challenge is to improve task performance without degrading the generalization capabilities of the model. In this paper, we present an extensive set of ablations for fine-tuning Qwen3-8B with low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We compare three training regimes: (1) response-only LoRA, where the supervised response is the label alone; (2) single-adapter reasoning, where reasoning traces from a teacher model are included alongside the labels in the…

items.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
items.summary: Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. They nevertheless remain brittle on long-horizon, contact-rich tasks in real-world environments. Further progress depends on two complementary resources: demonstrations of human behavior that supervise how tasks are performed, and interactive environments in which policies can be rolled out, evaluated, and improved in closed loop. Language models have advanced along well-characterized scaling laws; the corresponding question for physical AI is how capability scales with environments and behaviors, which first requires identifying which data to scale…

items.title: De Sitter Gravity and Emergent Time from Fusion Matrix Product States and SYK
items.summary: We propose a quantum-mechanical model dual to two-dimensional de Sitter (dS) gravity. It is a quantum channel, defined by a matrix product state that fuses one spin at each step, and is related to a limit of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model without chord crossings. Its simplest part is a random walk with an emergent $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry, which we identify with the symmetry of the future boundary of dS. It selects a time variable in which the walk obeys the Schwarzian action and yields the disk amplitude of dS Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. As the simplest case, we consider free massless scalar fields in the fixed background of dS$_2$. We find the agreement of the two-point function in the…

items.title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
items.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on thousands of hours of recordings, yet their frozen features transfer poorly to downstream tasks, and this transfer does not consistently improve with larger models or more pretraining data. We show that a vision foundation model that has never seen EEG is a stronger frozen EEG encoder than these specialized models, once the signals are rendered as images that a vision transformer can read. Our method, SeeEEG, keeps the vision backbone frozen and learns only how EEG is displayed to it. Each channel occupies a dedicated row of patches and is drawn either as a waveform at a fixed gain or as a scalogram whose frequency range…

items.title: Spin to win: enhancing the quantum Otto cycle with the circular Unruh effect
items.summary: We study a quantum Otto cycle whose working medium is a qubit Unruh-DeWitt detector undergoing uniform circular motion in $(3+1)$-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, interacting with a massless scalar field in a thermal state during the isochoric strokes. We compute the detector's transition rate and determine its energy gap-dependent effective temperature, showing that the effective temperature can be higher than the ambient bath temperature in the small energy gap limit and lower in the high bath temperature limit. We then investigate how these motion-induced effective temperatures affect the operating conditions and performance of the quantum Otto cycle as a heat engine or a refrigerator.…

items.title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how biological research is done. Biological foundation models trained on millions of nucleotides, protein, and single-cell measurements predict protein structures, mutation effects, and cellular responses to genetic perturbations. Agentic systems, AI assistants built on large language models, can run multistep analyses from plain-language requests and increasingly call foundation models as tools. Yet it is often unclear when these models' outputs can be trusted. We frame this as a model's knowledge boundary: the range of inputs, tasks, and conditions over which its outputs are reliable. This review explains how foundation models are built and…

items.title: Compiling Known Rules into Compact Neural Agents: Weight-Space Programming on Unseen Games
items.summary: Weight-space programming (WSP) uses language models to construct neural network weights without training. We test whether known game mechanics can be compiled into compact agents that generalise to held-out levels, renderings and start states within a game family. Writers receive simulator source with held-out level data removed for 20 privately authored, unpublished ARC-AGI-3-style game families. With a fixed 57k-parameter recurrent architecture, the strongest writer reaches 56% held-out-level success with feedback, while the four main writers' Python players reach 97-100%. An exploratory free-architecture condition reaches 68-90%. Learning from support-level examples transfers much less…

items.title: Universal Infectious Disease Forecasting with Mantis 2
items.summary: Public health agencies need to anticipate how outbreaks will unfold, when they will peak, and how long demand on health services will remain elevated. We previously developed a foundation model, Mantis, which was trained entirely on simulated outbreaks---enabling us to generate the diversity and scale of training data needed to support forecasting across diseases. However, our previous work left unresolved when simulation improves predictions and how it should complement observational data. Here, we varied the balance of simulated and observed training data while holding forecasting tasks fixed and varying the available surveillance history. We found that simulation-rich training was…

items.title: Time Flies When You Parallelise: Pareto-efficient Time Series Foundation Models with Linear Recurrences

items.summary: We present Kosmo-GFM, a scene reconstruction system that integrates a geometry foundation model (GFM), a pose optimization engine (PoseEngine), and reconstruction-derived supervision from KosmoWorld. items.summary: Reliable protection under varying power system operating conditions requires rapid fault detection while preserving selectivity against external faults and non-fault disturbances. items.summary: Protection of converter-dominated distribution networks is challenging due to limited fault currents, operating-mode transitions, bidirectional power flow, and heterogeneous network configurations. items.title: Multifunctional vortex magnetic tunnel junctions with optical and radio-frequency inputs for neuromorphic computing
items.summary: Abstract The brain co-locates memory and processing, but many neuromorphic devices need standby power or separate memory from nonlinear computation. items.summary: Background The global trend of population ageing is progressively worsening, leading to an increasing prevalence of dysphagia among the elderly population. items.summary: Abstract Universities are adopting artificial intelligence through cloud platforms, enterprise assistants, learning systems, research tools, and administrative analytics, yet most institutions lack a method for judging whether these arrangements preserve meaningful digital autonomy. This methodological paper develops the University AI Sovereignty Index (UASI), a multidimensional assessment of an institution's practical capacity to choose, govern, scrutinise, and, when necessary, exit AI dependencies. items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.summary: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch.…

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.summary: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.summary: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.summary: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). items.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
items.summary: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. items.title: Running out of Field Range: Nonlinear Sourcing of Light Scalars
items.summary: Light scalar fields coupled linearly to the Standard Model are constrained by equivalence-principle tests, fifth-force searches, clock comparison tests, and stellar cooling. These bounds assume that the coupling to ordinary matter can be expanded to linear order for all field values reached. For a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson with decay constant $f$ this fails as soon as the field value reaches $O(f)$. The field around a source then stops growing with the coupling, and in addition the linear coupling of a probe is suppressed depending on its location. items.title: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models
items.summary: We use TabPFN, a recently developed tabular foundation model, to predict three properties of energetic materials: impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature and crystal density. Without any hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN outperforms the best published models for all three properties. It also substantially outperforms a wide range of established machine-learning models, including tuned gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forests and Gaussian processes. This holds both when the models are given hand-crafted molecular descriptors and when they are given learned representations from Chemprop's message-passing neural network. items.title: Metric-Aligned Group Relative Policy Optimization for Explainable Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Deepfake detectors are commonly evaluated on real/fake classification alone, but real-world applications require explanations of the visual evidence behind each prediction. Joint vision-language models struggle with authenticity assessment, producing "real" narratives for manipulated images. To address this, we propose a decoupled predict-then-explain pipeline as our submission to the ACM Multimedia 2026 Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge, with methods trained and evaluated on the XPlainVerse benchmark. items.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
items.summary: Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are increasingly used in sensor applications, where sampling frequency (SF) varies across sensors, devices, and operating modes (e.g., power saving). Ideally, TSFMs must remain effective during such SF changes, provided the SF retains task-critical bandwidth. In this paper, we stress-test 4 prominent TSFMs: MOMENT, Chronos-2, Moirai-MoE, and TimesFM, to quantify their SF-invariance and investigate whether their behavior tracks the resulting loss of information bandwidth rather than the SF value itself. items.title: OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models
items.summary: Video world models promise general-purpose interactive simulators, but their training is limited by action supervision: action labels are scarce, fragmented across incompatible specifications, and do not scale with the unlabeled video pretraining corpus. A common workaround jointly trains an action encoder to compress consecutive frames into a latent action and a decoder to reconstruct the next frame from the previous frame and that latent, forcing the latent to capture only new information. items.title: Exploring Post-Hoc Disentanglement of Audio Foundation Models for Music Similarity
items.summary: Audio foundation models like CLAP, MuQ, and MERT excel at capturing general musical similarity. On the other hand, their entangled latent spaces limit interpretability and fine-grained attribute control. Conditional Similarity Networks (CSN) address this by pairing a backbone representation model with learned masks that gate the embedding space into attribute-specific subspaces. items.summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast unseen series without task-specific training. Increasingly they are built on recurrent backbones, whose constant per-step cost makes long-context inference cheap, and which, unlike transformers, carry a state. items.summary: Remote-sensing foundation models increasingly unify representations across sensing modalities and downstream tasks, yet their prediction mechanisms remain largely task-specific. Separate decoders, prediction heads, and objectives leave prediction fragmented across tasks. This naturally raises a question: can heterogeneous remote-sensing tasks share the prediction process? items.title: Fine-Tuning an Order-Flow Foundation Model for Sub-Second Forecasting

items.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
items.summary: Foundation models such as GPT and Claude have shown strong capabilities in spatial understanding and embodied intelligence. In particular, a set of statistical procedures is developed and implemented to characterize the statistical properties of the background noise for a subnetwork of $N$ Galileo satellite clocks, including a false-alarm rate estimation and a detection efficiency analysis. These methods allow to implement a coincidence analysis and establish a preliminary statistical framework for a robust and controlled search for domain-wall crossings in clock data, and for deriving constraints on…

items.title: How Many Exposures Does a World Model Need? Learning Unseen Game Mechanics at Test Time
items.summary: World models enable agents to plan and learn from imagined experience, but in an unfamiliar environment they must learn its mechanics from limited interaction. A mechanic is a rule for how an action or an interaction changes part of the environment. Each occurrence of a mechanic that the model observes is one exposure. We ask how many exposures a world model needs to predict the effects of a new environment's mechanics. We address this question on ARC-AGI-3, a benchmark of interactive games defined by their programs. We introduce MechEval, which labels 69 recurring mechanics across 20 games from these programs. It scores each prediction on the cells the mechanic changes at each exposure.…

items.title: PACE-ECG: Patient-Aware Contrastive ECG Pretraining; Leveraging Longitudinal Structure for Transferable Representations
items.summary: Foundation models for physiological signals are commonly evaluated on in-domain interpretation tasks, but their ability to transfer to longitudinal clinical prognosis across healthcare systems remains uncertain. We developed PACE-ECG, an ECG pretraining framework that combines contrastive learning across temporally neighbouring recordings from the same patient with clinically guided multitask supervision. We evaluated frozen ECG representations for post-myocardial-infarction all-cause mortality and incident heart failure prediction across MIMIC-IV and two external HEEDB cohorts, comparing the proposed representation with DeepECG-SSL, a state-of-the-art model, and two control baselines.…

items.title: Zeta function in Coulomb background
items.summary: We calculate the one-loop vacuum energy of a massive scalar field confined to the interior of a sphere with Dirichlet boundary conditions and subject to a Coulomb background potential $α/r$. The spectrum is determined by the zeros of a confluent hypergeometric (Kummer) function, and the corresponding zeta function is constructed and analytically continued to $s=-1/2$. The renormalization is performed by subtracting the divergent part of the zeta function, defined through the heat kernel expansion, which removes the non-decreasing powers of the mass and leaves a finite, physically normalized vacuum energy. items.title: A forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models: an EFM3D case study for crime scene reconstruction
items.summary: Foundation models increasingly combine geometry, semantics, and spatial context for three-dimensional scene understanding, but their suitability for forensic crime scene reconstruction remains unclear. This study presents a structured forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models and demonstrates it using the Egocentric Foundation Model for 3D (EFM3D). Four simulated indoor crime scenes were recorded with Meta Project Aria Gen~1 at Robert Gordon University's East Lodge House forensic training facility. items.summary: Large-scale representation learning has produced public foundation models that provide strong general-purpose visual features. However, their pretraining objectives are not designed for robot representation learning, so the resulting embeddings tend to emphasize global semantics rather than the temporally sensitive representations required for robot control. items.title: TSFFormer: A Frequency-Domain Spike Transformer for Green Human Activity Recognition
items.summary: Wearable Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) enable pervasive Human Activity Recognition (HAR), but traditional Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) suffer from an "arithmetic-latency deadlock" due to dense floating-point MAC operations. items.summary: Embodied navigation requires agents to achieve persistent spatial awareness and long-horizon execution stability in open-world environments. However, existing navigation architectures struggle to sustain both capabilities, remaining effective only over a handful of recent frames. We present Compass 1, the first embodied navigation foundation model to unify language understanding and video generation while enabling memory backtracking through nearly 2mins of visual history. items.title: Next-Generation Segmentation in Radiotherapy: A Narrative Review from Atlas-Based Methods to Agentic Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Precise segmentation of target volumes and organs at risk is an essential prerequisite for modern, high-precision radiation therapy. However, this task has traditionally been time-consuming and subject to high interobserver variability. Motivated by these limitations, more advanced and novel approaches to automating this task have been developed over the past two decades. This narrative review highlights representative milestones, with a focus on the most recent developments. items.summary: Accurate prediction of molecular reactivity requires both accurate and computationally efficient description of electron correlation and spin across various molecular geometries and electronic states. We introduce SATE, a spin-adapted transferable neural wavefunction architecture with effective core potentials. SATE combines a transferable neural wavefunction, the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, and effective core potentials into a single foundation model architecture pretrained on compositions containing selected elements from hydrogen to bromine. items.summary: Zero-shot object-goal navigation requires autonomous agents to explore unseen environments and locate target objects without task-specific training, posing challenges in perceptual reliability under observation uncertainty and physically grounded goal termination. Although foundation-model-based approaches improve generalization, they remain vulnerable to unreliable long-range perception, hallucination-induced directional bias, and semantically plausible but geometrically incorrect stopping decisions. items.title: OriDynamics: Towards a World Model for Biomolecular Dynamics
items.summary: Biomolecular recognition and regulation depend on atomic interactions that change as molecular partners fluctuate and adopt alternative conformations. Modeling these processes requires ensembles that capture both conformational diversity and coordinated atomic fluctuations between interacting molecules. Here we present OriDynamics, a unified framework for all-atom ensemble generation across protein monomers and complexes with small molecules or protein partners. OriDynamics introduces a latent ensemble decomposition that couples broad conformational exploration in a compact structural latent space with local all-atom sampling around generated proposals. items.title: Optimal asymptotic pure-state conversion under thermal operations
items.summary: Quantum thermodynamics seeks to characterize possible state transformations under thermodynamic constraints in microscopic quantum systems. In the fully quantum regime, however, quantum coherence imposes various restrictions on state conversions, and a complete characterization of state convertibility has remained open. Here we resolve this problem for asymptotic conversions between pure states. Specifically, we show that asymptotic convertibility is fully determined by the free-energy and energy-variance ratios. Our result reveals how genuinely quantum effects quantitatively constrain state conversions in quantum thermodynamics.
