Tunable magnetotransport through kinetically arrested first-order phase transitions in an antiferromagnetic metal
items.summary: Controllable multilevel resistance states are of interest for memory technologies like neuromorphic computing, but robust materials platforms toward such behavior remain limited. Here, we show that the non-centrosymmetric antiferromagnetic metal CeCoGe$_3$ suggests one such route through a kinetically hindered first-order magnetic transition. Cooling through the kinetically hindered first-order transition in an applied magnetic field produces a magnetic glass state in which high- and low-temperature magnetic phases coexist. The relative fraction of these phases can be controlled by the applied field in which the sample is cooled, and the electrical resistance is directly sensitive to that…

items.title: Probing EEG Foundation Model Attention Maps for Lightweight Interpretable Emotion Recognition
items.summary: Foundation Models (FMs) trained on EEG signals promise subject- and dataset-independent pipelines for brain-computer interface (BCI) applications, but have yet to consistently outperform task-specific architectures, and their large representations are costly to compute and store. As a means of advancing the understanding of the Foundation Models' inner mechanisms, we propose a lightweight alternative that exploits the self-attention mechanism of REVE, a pretrained EEG FM, to derive features similar to weighted Functional Connectivity (FC) without any fine-tuning. Inspired by kernel-based FC matrices, we aggregate the raw first-layer attention weights of a single head over the full duration…

items.title: A gait foundation model for prediction of multisystem health phenotypes from 3D skeletal motion.
items.summary: Gait is increasingly recognized as a vital sign, yet current approaches treat it as a symptom of specific pathologies rather than a systemic biomarker. Here we developed a gait foundation model for three-dimensional skeletal motion, which was recorded via a single-depth camera during 5 motor tasks, from 3,328 deeply phenotyped adults. Our purpose was to capture the full pattern of a person's movement and use it to predict health phenotypes such as grip strength and sleep quality across 18 body systems. Gait is conventionally described by engineered features (for example, calculated measurements such as cadence and stride length), which may fail to capture the fine detail of how a person…

items.title: Unimodal imaging foundation models and vision-language models in MRI: A systematic review of emerging methods and clinical applications.
items.summary: Artificial intelligence in medical imaging is shifting from task-specific algorithms toward adaptable foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). However, applying these models to MRI remains challenging because clinical interpretation requires integrating multi-parametric, volumetric imaging across multiple sequences with clinical context. This systematic review evaluates 35 studies on unimodal FMs and multimodal VLMs in MRI, summarizing emerging architectures, downstream applications, and challenges to clinical translation. Current research is concentrated in neuroimaging, with diagnostic classification representing the most mature application. Segmentation and outcome…

items.title: Segmentation-perturbation propagation in pretrained foundation-model embeddings versus IBSI-aligned radiomics for radiologist-assessed lung-nodule malignancy classification on the LIDC-IDRI cohort.
items.summary: Objective Pretrained foundation-model (FM) embeddings are proposed as robust alternatives to handcrafted radiomic features, yet whether they better withstand segmentation-mask variability, the perturbation that radiomics intraclass-correlation (ICC) filtering exists to address, has not been tested head-to-head. We quantified how segmentation-mask perturbation propagates into feature reproducibility and downstream malignancy discrimination for FM embeddings and Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative (IBSI)-compliant radiomics measured on a common cohort. Approach. Two 2D FM encoders (BiomedCLIP; RadImageNet ResNet50) were compared against IBSI-compliant radiomics (3D, 107 features; 2D,…

items.title: Quantifying multi-lesion detection and localization in whole-body FDG PET/CT with a multimodal foundation model.
items.summary: ObjectiveTo develop a 3D AI framework for detecting and localizing multiple lesions in whole-body FDG PET/CT, and to evaluate whether a pretrained PET/CT foundation model can improve lesion detection performance compared with conventional training from scratch.ApproachThe AutoPET cohort comprised 1,014 studies divided into 700 training, 114 validation, and 200 subject-independent test studies. Tumor masks were converted into 3D bounding boxes. We developed a one-stage 3D lesion detector using a PlainConvUNet backbone to extract multi-scale encoder-decoder features for lesion classification and box regression. To leverage foundation-model representations, the PlainConvUNet backbone was…

items.title: World Foundation Models and Agentic AI in Medicine: Physiological Simulation, Digital Twins, and Clinical Decision-Making.
items.summary: Many foundation models that have entered medicine are language models, although foundation models for imaging and other modalities have also emerged. A second class is now emerging from robotics and autonomous driving, trained not to produce text but to predict how an environment evolves under action, and marketed under the designation world foundation model. We argue that medicine should approach this class with a specific form of caution. Medicine already possesses world models in the mechanistic simulators and digital twins built from physiology and physics, and the constraint on those has never been the volume of available data. The constraint is identifiability. A simulator learned…

items.title: Researchers' perspectives on donor-level metadata collection and reporting for human tissue research.
items.summary: Introduction No widely adopted guidelines exist for collecting and reporting donor-level metadata in tissue-based research, which limits interpretability and reproducibility and may introduce bias. This study aimed to identify researchers' perspectives to inform ethical and appropriate metadata practices. Materials and methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 investigators from the Human BioMolecular Atlas Program. Thematic analysis using inductively derived codes identified metadata elements and perspectives on their collection and reporting. Results Participants identified 80 metadata variables across six domains: demographic, sociodemographic, medical history,…

items.title: A full-hardware edge detection system based on a highly robust dual random number generator.
items.summary: Conventional edge computing hardware at autonomous driving terminals is limited by chip area and power efficiency for complex image data. Recently, researchers have used memristors to construct dedicated hardware systems, achieving advancements in multiple image processing fields such as pattern recognition and edge detection. However, a full-hardware image processing system with anti-interference, low power, and high real-time performance remains challenging. Here, we fabricated a volatile Ag/AlO x /n-Si memristor with exceptional stability and low power. High-resolution electron microscopy visualized Ag conductive filament formation. Integrating two memristors with a logic circuit, we…

items.title: Ferroionic-Assisted, Charge-Driven Polymorphic Phase Engineering for Multilevel Memristive Devices.
items.summary: Memristive device operation can arise from diverse microscopic mechanisms, including charge polarization and trapping, magnetic ordering, ionic migration, and structural phase transitions. Among these, crystalline-crystalline phase transitions in polymorphic materials offer a unique platform for nonvolatile resistance modulation but are often hindered by large energy barriers and limited endurance. Here, we demonstrate a multimodal, charge-driven phase modulation in an atomically thin polymorphic material, Mo 0.92 W 0.08 Te 2 , enabled by electrostatic coupling to a ferroionic substrate, CuInP 2 S 6 . The polymorphic channel exhibits reversible switching between semiconducting and metallic…

items.title: Extrapolation Matters: Sparse-Only Depth Completion Beyond LiDAR Coverage
items.summary: Extrapolation beyond LiDAR coverage is an important yet under-evaluated challenge of depth completion. In real camera--LiDAR systems, partial sensor overlap, occlusions, and limited field coverage often leave large image regions weakly observed or completely unobserved by LiDAR. Thus, we investigate depth completion in this beyond-coverage regime using only sparse supervision from raw single-sweep LiDAR, without dense depth labels, LiDAR accumulation, or pseudo-LiDAR generation. Our approach leverages a frozen monocular depth foundation model, lightweight per-frame alignment to sparse LiDAR geometry, and a refinement module that fuses the aligned prior with sparse LiDAR anchors to predict…

items.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
items.summary: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. As these systems become more capable and autonomous, their potential to cause societal harm also grows, making AI safety one of the defining challenges of our time. Yet we continue to build increasingly powerful systems without fully understanding how they work, how they will behave in unfamiliar situations, or how to reliably control them. Mechanistic interpretability offers a path towards understanding these systems by studying their internal representations and computations, with the aim of evaluating, predicting, and controlling behaviour. We survey mechanistic interpretability for AI safety in…

items.title: Synaptic Multi-Weight Wafer-Scale Domain Wall Magnetic Tunnel Junctions Driven by Spin Orbit Torque
items.summary: Spintronic synaptic devices based on magnetic random access memory (MRAM) are a rapidly evolving class within the analog neuromorphic architecture. However, obtaining the multi-weight or analog behavior desired for improved neural network inference accuracy in scaled MRAM remains a challenge. In this study, we demonstrate and tune up to eight distinct resistance levels in 300 mm wafer-scale magnetic tunnel junction artificial synapses driven by spin orbit torque. By varying the applied in-plane field, multi-weight resistance states emerge through domain wall nucleation and pinning. These multi-weight states appear stochastically and can be addressed with an iterative programming algorithm…

items.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
items.summary: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes…

items.title: OraRefer: Segmentation-Guided Multi-Photograph Fusion for Oral Cancer Screening with Guaranteed Patient-Level Sensitivity
items.summary: Oral cancer and the oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) that can precede it are visible on the oral mucosa, which makes smartphone photographs a promising tool for screening. Deep learning models for this task classify individual photographs. However, screening refers patients, not photographs: a patient is usually photographed several times, and the referral decision must miss no more than a set share of patients with disease. We propose OraRefer, a patient-level screening model that reads each photograph with a segmentation-guided foundation model that conditions its class decision on the predicted lesion, combines all photographs of a patient with risk factors, and refers…

items.title: Instabilities of Simpson-Visser black bounces sourced by a phantom scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics
items.summary: We study the linear stability of Simpson-Visser ``black-bounce'' space-times (regular black holes and wormholes) under spherically symmetric (monopole) perturbations, taking as a source a phantom scalar field with a self-interaction potential and a magnetic field within nonlinear electrodynamics (NED). The metric contains two parameters: the mass $M$ and the bounce parameter $a >0$, such that $a \leq 2M$ corresponds to black holes and $a > 2M$ to wormholes. The stability problem reduces to a boundary-value problem for a Schrödinger-like equation with a certain effective potential. All space-times under study are found to be unstable, and the corresponding exponential growth rates are…

items.title: Do sEMG Foundation Models Improve Cross-Subject Generalisation?
items.summary: sEMG Foundation Models aim to learn general purpose representations over diverse subjects and recording conditions that boost performance on a variety of downstream tasks. However, existing evaluations make it difficult to discern whether pretraining alone is sufficient to combat the cross-subject overfitting which makes machine learning on sEMG so challenging. We conduct a systematic evaluation of three sEMG foundation models across three gesture classification datasets under both intra-session and inter-subject splits, using three fine-tuning strategies designed to isolate the contribution of pretraining. We find that pretraining boosts performance when train and test samples are drawn…

items.title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks
items.summary: Tokamak experiments record diverse measurements, including waveforms, profiles, fields, and scalars, which are used to reconstruct the plasma, forecast its evolution, recover associated control signals, and estimate disruption risk. Most models are built separately for one task and a fixed set of inputs and outputs, and each relies on a prescribed subset of diagnostics rather than structuring the full multimodal observation set to extract global, cross-signal information about the discharge. These limitations motivate a reusable foundation model that adapts to each task's input-output schema and models heterogeneous target signals jointly, rather than retraining a separate model for every…

items.title: Who Can Evaluate AI Independently? A Framework for Analysing Evaluation Infrastructure
items.summary: AI evaluation is increasingly central to AI safety and governance, yet taking part in an evaluation does not by itself confer authority over its design, its execution or the resources it depends on. This paper examines how infrastructure arrangements distribute that authority, and so shape who can evaluate AI systems independently. Drawing on Science and Technology Studies, political economy and applied evaluation standards, we introduce PAAI (Power, Access, Adequacy, Independence), a framework for examining who controls evaluation infrastructure, the terms on which it is available, whether it is adequate to the evaluation's purpose and what autonomy it supports. We apply PAAI to twelve…

items.title: Route-DMD: Distribution Matching Distillation with Task-Routed Mechanism for Speech Foundation Models
items.summary: Speech foundation models built on flow matching handle generation, editing, and processing in one system, but every request costs 20-50 iterative steps, and classifier-free guidance (CFG) doubles each of them. Distribution matching distillation (DMD) trains a student that approaches the teacher's quality in a few steps, yet existing speech distillation work applies it to generation alone. We show that a distribution-matching objective does not serve every task: in separation, the noised states of erroneous student outputs deviate far from the teacher's training distribution, where its prediction is unreliable. Route-DMD therefore makes the objective task-dependent, routing the affected…

items.title: When GeoFMs Meet VHR: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Very High Resolution Earth Observation Imagery
items.summary: Geospatial foundation models are a widely adopted starting point for remote sensing tasks. Most are pretrained on Sentinel-1/2 and Landsat imagery at a ground sampling distance (GSD) of 10m or coarser. Many applications instead rely on very high resolution (VHR) imagery, where individual buildings, roads, and amenities are resolved. We study which pretraining regimes transfer well to this scale. We introduce VHR-Bench, a benchmark suite of ten datasets at 1.5m GSD or finer spanning five task families, eight application domains, and both satellite and aerial platforms. We evaluate twelve encoders in three pretraining tiers with frozen backbones at two training-data fractions. We find that…

items.title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
items.summary: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|α\rangle$. We demonstrate that single-photon-added coherent…

items.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
items.summary: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $ξ$-attractors, in which a single function $f(φ)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(φ)$ which is $f'(φ)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(φ)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate. We classify the poles and…

items.title: Log-concavity and level set curvature estimates for the first Dirichlet eigenfunction in hyperbolic space
items.summary: In this paper, we study the first Dirichlet eigenfunction on bounded, smooth and strictly horo-convex domains in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We prove its strict $\log$-concavity in arbitrary dimension and establish the Gauss curvature bound $K>1$ for its level sets. In dimensions two and three, we further obtain quantitative lower bounds for $K$ in terms of the minimum Gauss curvature of the boundary. In higher dimensions, the product of the two smallest principal curvatures of each level hypersurface exceeds one. Furthermore, we extend the strict $\log$-concavity result to bounded smooth horo-convex domains. Our approach combines maximum or minimum principles for suitable auxiliary…

items.title: When, Where, How: Active In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) adapt to a new task only through the labeled rows in their context. However, labels are expensive to acquire in real-world scenarios due to the need for highly specific domain knowledge to ensure high-quality data. Active in-context learning transfers classical acquisition rules to this setting, in which the model that guides acquisition changes with every label added. We ask how the value of diversity, predictive uncertainty and target-aware information gain changes as a frozen TFM acquires more context. For that, we study Target-Aware Nearest Neighbor (TANN) acquisition and the Expected Predictive Information Gain in Context (EPIC) and evaluate them…

items.title: InnerLogic-Surg: An Open Surgical Foundation Model via Continual Pretraining
items.summary: Vision foundation models are the backbone of modern surgical image analysis, yet most surgical systems still rely on encoders pretrained on natural images or on specialist models trained from scratch on comparatively small datasets. Pretraining encoders on large amounts of surgery-specific data has the potential to generally enhance the performance of surgical image analysis methods simply by providing stronger backbones. Here we present InnerLogic-Surg, an open family of surgical vision encoders (21M--300M parameters) obtained by continually pretraining a transformer-based image encoder on millions of surgical images curated from 11,965 internet-sourced surgical videos spanning ~2,900…

items.title: Responsible GenAI Use During Active Armed Conflict: Evidence from Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms
items.summary: Armed conflict can increase the value of Generative AI (GenAI) while undermining the conditions required for its responsible use. Yet the perspectives of community-based humanitarian responders working under these conditions remain underrepresented in responsible AI research. We examine GenAI use in Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs), a community-led humanitarian network, through an exploratory survey of 89 respondents and 15 semi-structured interviews with GenAI users and non-users. War reconfigures GenAI's role, making it most useful where its outputs are hardest to verify. ERR responders turned to GenAI when conflict made human expertise difficult or dangerous to reach. However,…

items.title: Scenario-aware Adaptive Neuromorphic Intelligence for multimodal sensor fusion
items.summary: Multisensory Physical AI systems operating in isolated conditions must make timely and reliable decisions within strict energy and hardware budgets. In this context, the present analytical study investigates the feasibility of reliable multimodal sensor fusion using a neuromorphic approach based on memristor-based Integrate-and-Fire neuron circuits driven by aggressively compressed representations of sensory information. Rather than relying on fixed processing and learning parameters, the proposed framework introduces scenario-dependent adaptability into individual stages of the neuromorphic decision-making pipeline, including sensor-data compression, nonlinear spike encoding, reliability…

items.title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
items.summary: Energy forecasting models are usually compared on backtests and fixed public datasets. Backtests can use data that did not yet exist when the forecast would have been made, and a fixed test set, reused across studies and possibly contained in the pretraining data of foundation models, invites overfitting to the benchmark. EnergyBench evaluates every entry live instead. Each day at 11:30 CET/CEST, thirty minutes before the day-ahead (SDAC) gate closes, every model forecasts the next day's price, wind and solar generation and load on the 15-minute grid for six bidding zones (BE, NL, FR, DE-LU, DK1, DK2). Unlike existing live benchmarks, EnergyBench runs the models itself, on one information…

items.title: Pediatric ECG foundation model via adult-to-pediatric fine-tuning: downstream tasks and clinical evaluation
items.summary: Pediatric electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation is complicated by age-dependent electrophysiological changes that limit direct transfer of adult AI models. We asked whether an adult ECG foundation model could be adapted to pediatric ECGs. Using 339,563 12-lead ECGs from 238,189 children, we compared direct application, pediatric fine-tuning, and training from scratch under an identical architecture. Direct transfer was poor (mean AUC 0.8256). Fine-tuning reached 0.9695, above de novo training (0.9661), and attained 0.9079 using only 1% of training data. On 10,999 external ECGs, fine-tuning achieved a mean AUC of 0.9385 across 30 labels. It generalized to age regression (MAE 1.12 years)…

items.title: Real-Time Event-Based LED Tracking and Pose Estimation with PWM-Encoded Markers
items.summary: Event cameras are neuromorphic vision sensors with pixels that independently and asynchronously respond to brightness changes at microsecond resolution, supporting state estimation under rapid motion, motion blur, and high dynamic range (HDR) illumination. This also enables capture of high-frequency blinking patterns from light-emitting diodes (LEDs). Based on this, we propose a real-time event-based framework for LED tracking and six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) relative pose estimation using pulse-width modulation (PWM)-encoded LED markers. Multiple LEDs share a common blinking frequency and encode identities through distinct PWM duty cycles, reducing frequency-resource requirements and…

items.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
items.summary: Agent harness evolution enables recursive self-improvement (RSI) without updating model weights. We examine whether higher benchmark scores yield reliable, efficient, and transferable improvement. We evaluate four methods across harnesses, general and coding tasks. Repeated evaluations, controlled agent expansion, component interventions, and admission replays reveal recurring patterns. All sixteen evolved agents gain previously uncovered tasks while losing previously covered ones. In one general-task case, reliability rises by 5.2 points despite losing ten previously covered tasks. Most reliability gains also increase deployment cost. Specific changes usually outperform generic reminders,…

items.title: Evolver: Turning Agent Exploration into Evolving Capabilities
items.summary: Agent exploration produces valuable procedural knowledge, yet much of this experience remains confined to transient execution traces and is not systematically reused. We introduce Evolver, an experience-driven framework that transforms agent exploration into persistent, reusable capabilities without updating foundation model parameters. Built around structured Gene assets, Evolver integrates experience acquisition, retrieval, and feedback-guided evolution to support experience-conditioned execution across existing agent harnesses. We evaluate Evolver using Claude Code and Codex, two foundation model configurations, and four benchmarks: Terminal-Bench 2.1, SWE-bench Multilingual,…

items.title: Recursive Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue
items.summary: Long-horizon role-playing dialogue requires consistent character identity, reliable memory, and context-sensitive interaction. We present a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) framework that revises original-character memory, stable persona instructions, and a policy for constructing turn-level prompts. Repair outcomes also inform revisions to the updater's diagnostic rules, edit routing, and candidate selection. We specify the updater as a versioned policy with explicit inputs, editable fields, acceptance gates, and stopping conditions. An internal evaluation covers 50 original characters and five models, with two 100-round conversations per character-model pair: 500 conversations…

items.title: IMUDINO: Self-distilled Foundation Model for Inertial Sensing
items.summary: We present IMUDINO, the first foundation model (FM) for inertial sensing to achieve competitive performance across diverse sensing tasks including human activity recognition (HAR), health, motion capture, and odometry. Prior inertial FMs often focus on one subfield of inertial sensing and sometimes underperform state-of-the-art supervised methods (e.g., in HAR), making their scope considerably narrower than FMs for vision and natural language. Moreover, they often require fixed input length and sampling rate, and generalize poorly to unseen sensor locations. To build a general-purpose foundation model for inertial sensing, we adapt the DINO self-supervised learning (SSL) paradigm to…

items.title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
items.summary: Symmetry governs the organization of physical structures, while symmetry breaking reveals their transformations. In geometric deep learning, symmetry imposes rank constraints on equivariant representations, limiting the expressive capacity of equivariant graph neural networks (GNNs). Here we show that these constraints can instead be exploited: the singular-value spectra of equivariant representations provide a unified fingerprint of structural symmetry. We introduce spectral symmetry fingerprints (SymFP), which enable discrete point-group identification through rank-template matching and continuous symmetry analysis by quantifying spectral energy beyond target rank constraints. SymFP is…

items.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
items.summary: We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. Equipping each path with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules provides sparse capacity, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated…

items.title: WeightLoop: Weight-Space Programming with Experimental Feedback
items.summary: Weight-space programming (WSP) shows that language models can reason about and rewrite neural network weights; recursive self-improvement (RSI) motivates feedback-driven improvement. Models guiding experiments receive concrete feedback: completed assays reveal prediction errors and inform what to test next. We introduce WeightLoop, a framework that turns experimental feedback into persistent updates to deployed predictors. GPT-6 Astra inspects a task specification and the model implementation, then writes a bounded, reusable parameter-editing program. As new measurements arrive, the program identifies prediction discrepancies, validates candidate edits using observed outcomes, and writes…

items.title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
items.summary: EHR foundation models read medical events within a fixed context window, and long context has so far been measured only in tokens. How far back in time a model must look to capture the earliest predictive signal is unknown. We introduce time-context, the calendar lookback window before the prediction point, and provide, to our knowledge, the first systematic evaluation of decade-scale time-context for an EHR foundation model. We pretrained a decoder-only transformer (34.6M parameters) on 1.4B coded events from 3.6M primary-care patients in North West London and fine-tuned it to predict incident colorectal cancer under a 12-month pre-diagnostic buffer. A frozen cohort of 1,008 cases and…

items.title: SoK: The Security-Safety Continuum of Multimodal Foundation Models
items.summary: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) integrate diverse data modalities to support complex and wide-ranging tasks. However, this integration also introduces distinct safety and security challenges. In this paper, we unify the concepts of safety and security in the context of MFMs by identifying critical threats that arise from both model behavior and system-level interactions. We propose a taxonomy grounded in information theory, evaluating risks through the concepts of channel capacity, signal, noise, and bandwidth. This perspective provides a principled way to analyze how information flows through MFMs and how vulnerabilities can emerge across modalities. Building on this foundation, we…

items.title: Mapping the Unmapped: A Structured Atlas of Human Futures with Artificial Superintelligence and the Cultural Visibility - SuperFutures Atlas
items.summary: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence toward artificial general intelligence (AGI) and potentially artificial superintelligence (ASI) has generated a vast, fragmented, and often contradictory discourse about humanity's future. This discourse spans academic research, policy documents, industry publications, online communities, and popular culture, but no systematic attempt has been made to catalogue, classify, and compare the full spectrum of scenarios being proposed. This paper presents the SuperFutures Scenario Atlas, a structured taxonomy of 55 distinct scenario families for the human–ASI relationship, each classified across identity, type, mechanism, time horizon, human…

items.title: SuperIntel Lab (sil): Scientific Tool Suite for Superintelligence Research
items.summary: A reproducible, three-layer scientific tool suite (micro behavioral evaluations, meso takeoff dynamics and thinking-pattern probes, macro Monte-Carlo risk decomposition and civilizational agent-based simulation) for studying the impacts of superintelligence, extinction/wipeout risk to humans, and AI thinking patterns and decision-making. All macro outputs are conditional projections under stated, cited priors (Carlsmith 2022, AI 2027 takeoff forecast, SysAdmin benchmark, MTAIR). Includes empirical profile fits to published rates, Wilson CIs, PRCC/Morris sensitivity analysis, a micro-to-macro calibration bridge, and publication-grade report generation.

items.title: HyPASE: Hyperbolic Geometry for Parameter-Efficient Speech Emotion Fine-Tuning Framework for Large Audio-Language Models
items.summary: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) excel at general speech understanding; however, adapting them to fine-grained tasks like Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) remains a significant bottleneck. Current Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods typically operate in flat Euclidean space, and this geometry fails to capture the multi-granularity nature of emotion cues, which range from low-level prosody to high-level semantics. To address this, we propose HyPASE, a hyperbolic PEFT framework for LALM-based SER. HyPASE leverages the Poincare ball model, using the hyperbolic radius as an explicit proxy for representational granularity. The framework consists of two core components: a…

items.title: Scale-Dependent Concordance of Poincaré and Tree-Based TAD Hierarchies and Its Coupling to A/B Compartmentalization in Isogenic Breast Cancer Cells
items.summary: Background: Hyperbolic embedding of Hi-C matrices into a Poincaré disc recovers the full TAD hierarchy from a single embedding. Two questions remain open: whether the hierarchy is method-independent, and whether the radial coordinate acquires new biological meaning upon neoplastic transformation.Results. items.title: Bridging Microtubules, Coherent Electromagnetic Field, and Consciousness
items.summary: Consciousness is proposed as a fundamental n-dimensional complex field which is intrinsically lossless, meaning it does not dissipate or lose information like physical systems do. This explains why subjective experience remains stable even when gravitational conditions change dramatically, such as for astronauts moving between Earth and Moon. Mind is defined as the interface between matter and consciousness. It has a physical origin in coherent electromagnetic fields in microtubules, as predicted by Fröhlich in 1968 who showed that biological systems under metabolic energy form Bose-like condensation of coherent vibrations, and by Popp since the 1970s who proved that living cells emit…

items.title: Spectraplakin is required for dendritic microtubule organization via a tip-based mechanism in Drosophila
items.summary: Abstract The differential microtubule organization in axons and dendrites underlies neuronal polarity and developmental processes like neurite pruning. How neurons achieve their specific microtubule organization during development is an area of active research, and it has been especially hard to explain how dendritic microtubules are oriented with their plus ends towards the soma. Transient microtubule nucleation from tips of early growing dendrites has been detected in some systems and would explain how orientation is set up. In a survey for cytoskeletal regulators involved in dendrite pruning and microtubule organization in Drosophila, we found the spectraplakin Short stop (Shot), an…

items.title: Microtubule stability modulates Schlemm’s canal cell mechanobiology and outflow facility in glaucoma
items.summary: Abstract Purpose The inner wall of Schlemm’s canal (SC) is a mechanosensitive endothelial monolayer that provides resistance to conventional aqueous humor drainage, a process dependent on pore formation. This study examined how microtubule (MT) stability affects SC cell mechanobiology, transcellular pore formation, and aqueous humor outflow dynamics. Methods MT stability in cultured SC cells from normal and glaucomatous human donors was manipulated pharmacologically. Changes in MT acetylation, phosphorylated myosin light chain, and F-actin were assessed by immunofluorescence and immunoblotting. GEF-H1 was knocked down using siRNA. Cellular stiffness was measured by atomic force microscopy.…

items.title: Neural Architecture Search of Time-to-First-Spike-Coded Spiking Neural Networks for Efficient Eye-based Emotion Recognition
items.summary: Eye-based emotion recognition enables eyewear devices to perceive users' emotional states and support emotion-aware interaction. However, deploying such functionality on their resource-limited embedded hardware remains challenging. Time-to-first-spike (TTFS)-coded spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a promising solution due to their extremely sparse and energy-efficient computation, where each neuron emits at most one binary spike. While prior works have primarily focused on improving TTFS SNN training algorithms, the role of network architecture has been largely overlooked. This is particularly critical, as spike timing in TTFS SNNs is tightly coupled with architectural design, and…

items.title: Image synthesis using spintronic deep convolutional generative adversarial network
items.summary: Abstract The computational requirements of generative adversarial networks (GANs) exceed the limit of conventional von neumann architectures, necessitating energy efficient alternatives such as neuromorphic spintronics. This work presents a hybrid CMOS-spintronic deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN) architecture for synthetic image generation. The proposed generative vision model approach follows the standard framework, leveraging generator and discriminators adversarial training, where key DCGAN operations including deconvolution, convolution, and activation are implemented using proposed spintronic hardware primitives. To enable hardware aware spintronic…

items.title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture.
items.summary: Escalating energy demands for high-performance machine learning have sparked growing interest in unconventional computing paradigms rooted in physical systems. Central to this direction is leveraging physical properties to design computing frameworks integrating strong learning capabilities, efficient training strategies and practical implementability. Here we present a simple, efficient and scalable framework aimed at achieving this, validated on an optoelectronic platform. This framework features our proposed training mechanism, state-skipping direct feedback alignment, together with our single-map architecture based on simple one-dimensional dynamics. The former eliminates the need to…

items.title: EventCLR: contrastive self-supervised learning for few-shot event-based vision using spiking neural networks
items.summary: Abstract Event-based vision sensors provide significant advantages for high-speed perception, including microsecond temporal resolution, high dynamic range, and low power consumption. When combined with Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), they are well suited to neuromorphic hardware and energy-efficient applications on embedded systems. However, this potential is severely limited by the scarcity of large-scale labeled datasets required to effectively train such models. In this work, we present EventCLR , a systematic approach to contrastive self-supervised learning for SNNs under label scarcity, a setting that closely matches the practical constraints of most real-world neuromorphic sensing…

items.title: Integration and annotation of spatial multi-omic data with DIRAC.
items.summary: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. DIRAC learns task-discriminative features that are insensitive to domain shifts caused by batch effects, omic modalities or study sites, enabling a shared embedding space and automated cell-type annotation through label transfer from reference datasets.…

items.title: Effective enzyme engineering through modeling kinetic parameter changes upon mutations with geometric deep learning
items.summary: Quantifying enzyme kinetic parameter changes upon mutations is essential for accelerating enzyme evolution. Current methods focus on predicting absolute values of kinetic parameters (turnover numbers kcat and Michaelis constants Km), yet they fail to accurately capture mutation effects. To our knowledge, no method directly models mutation effects (Δkcat and ΔKm) due to the scarcity of such training data. Moreover, these methods haven’t fully exploited protein structural geometry. Here, we establish a high-quality enzyme mutation effect dataset by pairing wild-type and mutant kinetic parameters measured under identical experimental conditions via a semi-automatic procedure combining…

items.title: Surgical Publicness in the Age of Artificial Intelligence : Rural Equity, Responsibility, and Dignity in Regional Surgical Care.
items.summary: The life sciences are being reorganized around computation, and this acceleration is reaching the operating theatre through decision support, computer vision, and increasingly autonomous robotic systems. Bioethical debate about surgical artificial intelligence (AI) has concentrated on safety, the diffusion of liability, and the patient before the algorithm. I argue that these debates leave a prior category underexamined: surgical publicness, the standing of surgical care as a public good that owes the population equitable access, a locatable line of clinical responsibility, and the preservation of human dignity. It sits where public health ethics, surgical ethics, and AI ethics meet,…

items.title: Where the Loop Meets the Budget: Analyzing On-Device Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Persistent self-improvement enables language-model agents to adapt from experience, but its update process competes with inference for limited device memory, energy, and thermal headroom. Existing surveys largely examine self-improvement mechanisms and on-device learning separately, providing limited guidance on how update reliability and device costs should be assessed together. We introduce a unified taxonomy that organizes persistent updates by component, execution locus, feedback, loop closure, timescale, and budget, and distinguishes recursive changes to evaluators or update machinery. Across the included works, we compare updates to memory and skills, prompts and code, weights, and…

items.title: Dark energy at the Compton threshold: a self-gravitating frozen vacuum confronted with DESI DR2
items.summary: Abstract Baryon acoustic oscillations from DESI DR2, combined with the cosmic microwave background and type Ia supernovae, prefer dark energy that is evolving away from w = −1. The simplest physical candidate is a thawing scalar field. We organise its physics around one dimensionless number, the expansion per tick of the field’s Compton clock, ε = ℏH/mc2 = m2 P /2MHm, where MH is the energy inside the Hubble sphere. Three results follow. (i) Exact solutions show that a coherent field turns from vacuum (w = −1) into matter (⟨w⟩ = 0) across the band 0.3 ≲ ε ≲ 2.2. (ii) We propose that the frozen vacuum sets its own clock, (mc2/ℏ) 2 = λ (8πG/3) ρfrozen, equivalently ε 2Ωfrozen = 1/λ: the…

items.title: Heterophase-Engineered Cs3Cu2I5/CsCu2I3 Memristors with Two-Step Resistive Switching.
items.summary: The quest for energy-efficient memory technologies is critically hindered by the performance gap between high-performing but toxic lead-based perovskites and their environmentally benign yet less reliable lead-free counterparts. Here, we address this challenge by engineering the controlled coexistence of crystallographically 0D Cs3Cu2I5 and 1D CsCu2I3 phases using a scalable, hot-air-assisted process. The resulting heterophase architecture produces composition-dependent structural, interfacial, and chemical environments that strongly influence resistive-switching behavior. The optimized devices exhibit a high ON/OFF ratio of up to 7.4 × 108, more than three orders of magnitude higher than…

items.title: Photoactive Nanocomposite Dielectric-Driven Low-Power All-Optical Organic Synaptic Transistors.
items.summary: Artificial optical synapses featuring low-energy consumption, high speed, and noise tolerance are critical for visual neuromorphic electronics. Most existing devices rely on complex multilayer structures or require high supply voltages to induce carrier tunneling effects. Therefore, we propose a photoactive nanocomposite dielectric (PND) layer, thereby enabling an embedded-layer-free, low-voltage, low-power optical organic synaptic transistor (OST) capable of all-optical, optical-electrical, and all-electrical modulation. We achieve this by functionalizing titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO 2 NPs) with nitrile butadiene rubber to fabricate a photo-curable, patternable PND layer. Under…

items.title: Conductive filament dynamics in memristive sensors: from resistive switching mechanisms to multifunctional sensing applications.
items.summary: With advances in sensor technology, various sensors are being widely applied, becoming an indispensable part of modern life. However, constrained by inherent sensing mechanisms, certain performance limitations remain difficult to improve through conventional modification methods. Herein, we focus on memristors for various sensing applications, summarizing how their resistive switching effect enables the modulation of device performance. First, the development history of memristors is outlined, and recent research progress in the fields of gas sensing, optoelectronic sensing, and pressure sensing is summarized. Meanwhile, representative memristors are employed as examples to investigate the…

items.title: How many labels can a biological oscillator carry? A quality-factor screen for proposed information carriers.
items.summary: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison. We show that spectral distinguishability alone bounds the number of labels by the quality factor, M≤Q=2πντ coh . It follows from the relation between linewidth and coherence time, is independent of substrate, mechanism and any position on quantum effects in biology, and can be evaluated from two published quantities. Applied to a recently proposed 30 GHz intracolumnar microwave field in cortex, it…

items.title: Goal Revelation as a Bridge Between Information-Theoretic Empowerment and Capability-Based Human Power
items.summary: Power matters for AI safety. Optimal agents tend to acquire power across a wide range of objectives (instrumental convergence). As we embed AI agents into socio-technical systems, humans risk gradual disempowerment. Both concerns call for a formal, quantitative measure of power. Two such measures in the context of Markov games are information-theoretic empowerment, the capacity of the channel from an agent's actions to future states, and capability-based individual power, a measure of goal attainment built from the probabilities that a human would attain each goal in a family of candidates were they pursuing it. We show where the two meet. From individual power, Fano's inequality yields a…

items.title: Backbone-Informed Adaptation after EEG Pretraining: A Capacity-Controlled Study
items.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models learn representations that combine information across channels and time. This structure motivates adapters that model the same relationships during downstream learning. However, it is not clear whether such a design outperforms other candidate adapters. Moreover, in order to arrive at a fair comparison between candidate adapters, we also need to consider their trainable parameters. Here, we ask whether a backbone-informed (native) adapter makes better use of a given capacity by comparing it against a token-wise multilayer perceptron control that transforms each feature vector independently. We approximately match their trainable parameter…

items.title: Scalar perturbations in two-scalar-field warm inflation
items.summary: We investigate scalar perturbations in a two-scalar-field cosmological model unifying warm inflation, dark matter, and dark energy. The inflaton is noncanonically coupled to a second scalar field that acts as dark energy at late times. Assuming negligible dissipation and perturbations of the dark-energy field, we derive the linear scalar perturbations in a gauge-ready form, including quantum and thermal noise in the inflaton sector and stochastic fluctuations of the energy transfer to radiation. We numerically solve the coupled perturbation system using a Fokker-Planck formalism and compute the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ for dissipation coefficients…

items.title: VINO: Revisiting 3D Representation Learning with Volume Transformers
items.summary: Self-supervised learning has given rise to vision foundation models that learn general-purpose image representations transferable across downstream tasks, yet representation learning for 3D scenes has not achieved comparable success. Motivated by this, we identify key limitations of current 3D representation learning approaches and revisit their core design choices. We first replace the commonly used hierarchical PTv3 backbone with the Volume Transformer, a ViT-like architecture for 3D scenes. We then redesign two core objectives of modern approaches built around student-teacher networks: matching representations across views and predicting masked content from visible context. For the…

items.title: Axial black hole perturbations in purely-metric Horndeski theories
items.summary: We study axial (odd-parity) perturbations about static and spherically-symmetric curvaturised black hole solutions of purely-metric Horndeski theories. We first review the construction of purely-metric theories of gravity with second-order equations of motion and an additional propagating scalar degree of freedom which is purely gravitational. We then revisit the formation, in a subclass of these theories, of a new branch of hairy black hole solutions under tachyonic instabilities of the scalar field near the Schwarzschild solution. Because a non-zero Ricci curvature grows and by analogy with black hole scalarisation, the latter black hole formation mechanism is dubbed…

items.title: CounterFactual Retrieval for Evidence-Aware Individual Animal Identification
items.summary: Automated identification of individual animals is moving from small curated studies toward shared benchmarks and reusable foundation models. This progress is useful, but current evaluation leaves the evidence behind a match unresolved, i.e., high retrieval accuracy does not show whether a model used animal features or identity-correlated shortcuts. We address this with Counterfactual Foreground Retrieval (CFR), an evidence-aware evaluation protocol. CFR evaluates the same query-gallery task under different views: full image, foreground-only, and shortcut-only. The full-image measures standard retrieval performance; the foreground-only measures foreground-supported retrieval; and…

items.title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement requires AI systems to improve the models and infrastructure used by subsequent systems. LLM compression offers a concrete efficiency objective: retain a pretrained model's behavior within a smaller model storage budget. We study whether coding agents can carry out this step autonomously. We formulate compression as a terminal task in which an agent receives a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget, then constructs compressed weights and executable inference code. The agent controls its algorithm and experiments; perplexity feedback guides search, and independent verification checks the final model. Across six agents and six…

items.title: Alignment Myopia in Generative AI
items.summary: Current generative AI alignment relies on a myopic paradigm that prioritizes immediate conversational satisfaction. By relying on short-horizon feedback, this approach ignores the profound, longitudinal externalities of persistent human-AI interaction, which can lead to adverse outcomes such as cognitive atrophy, social erosion, and diminished human agency. To address this, we propose a paradigm shift toward long-horizon alignment that accounts for how AI reshapes human experience over time. To this end, we map the tensions between near-term utility and long-term costs of AI use across four facets of human well-being to reveal outcomes that current reward models fail to capture.…

items.title: Rules, Traces and Routing Statistics: Training and Calibration Data for Open Models on ARC-AGI-2
items.summary: We study which training and calibration data help three open models solve ARC-AGI-2 tasks when the solver runs offline on four L4 GPUs for at most 12 hours. We compare data offline on public tasks and report 189 runs on the 120 hidden semi-private tasks. For the NVARC Qwen3-4B grid model, we built a corpus of 12,000 executable rules in a typed language and 95,993 tasks; a rule is admitted only if its behaviour on a fixed probe set differs from that of every admitted rule, and a task only if its pairs refute a shortlist of nearest competing rules and defeat 12 shortcut solvers. Continued fine-tuning on 1,920 real task records with revised four-GPU scheduling raised the semi-private score…

items.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanScale, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanScale-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these…

items.title: Transforming Integer Grids to Spatial Intuition: Perception, Not Planning, Governs ARC-AGI-3
items.summary: Sample-efficient fluid intelligence requires agents that rapidly form working models of unfamiliar interactive environments. ARC-AGI-3 tests this across uninstructed visual games scored by Relative Human Action Efficiency, which penalizes exploratory waste quadratically. When frontier models read raw integer grids, serialization destroys spatial topology, and they spend hundreds of actions rediscovering basic boundaries and symmetries. We introduce SARBLOH, an open-weight agent built on the premise that spatial perception, not planning capacity, governs interactive reasoning on ARC-AGI-3. A zero-parameter O(HW) perception engine turns each frame, in 35 ms, into an object inventory with…

items.title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World
items.summary: Coding agents powered by models such as GPT-6-Astra connect spatial reasoning with executable robot behavior, raising the question of how such agents can produce lasting improvements in robot capabilities from physical interaction. In this work, we study embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) through real-world exploration, code refinement, and deployment using PyRUA-REAL, a framework in which coding agents retain interaction experience as persistent memory and reusable executable skills that inform subsequent exploration and improvement. Our empirical study places physical manipulation at the center of the improvement process, examining how agents collaborate, what kinds of execution…

items.title: Inflationary attractors in metric-affine gravity
items.summary: We study single-field slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity (MAG). We consider the most general action up to operators linear in curvature and quadratic in the distortion, without propagating torsion and non-metricity. We first impose projective invariance and promote every coefficient to a function of the scalar field. After integrating out the non-dynamical distortion, the net contribution is a correction $k(φ)$ to the scalar kinetic term. We then consider the class of $ξ$-attractors for which the non-minimal couplings and the scalar potential are fixed by a single function $f(φ)$.
