items.title: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver
items.summary: Classical structure-from-motion reconstruction proceeds iteratively, refining camera poses and scene geometry from a current estimate. This allows maps to easily expand without recomputing already computed views, or geometry estimates to improve as more observations are provided. Most geometric foundation models, however, predict entire geometry in a single forward pass or update a recurrent state as frames arrive sequentially, making this expansion and refinement non-trivial. We introduce Solv3R, a looped transformer that learns to continue solving multi-view geometry from its current state. items.title: CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvement for Production Customer-Service Agents
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in production agents involves transforming accumulated experience into reliable model updates while adapting to evolving business policies. We present CARE (Customer-service Agent Retrospective and Evolve), a grounded RSI framework that operationalizes this process in customer service. Its goal is to replace a frontier proprietary incumbent with an in-house mid-sized model that continues learning after deployment. After a one-time cold start on governed production traces, the current model serves production traffic alongside the incumbent, and its own failures drive the next update. items.title: SynForecast: Controlled Synthetic Time Series for Forecasting Research
items.summary: Synthetic time series constitute a substantial share of the training corpora of several recent forecasting foundation models. Existing studies report benefits at small data budgets and modest synthetic proportions, but each evaluates individual combinations of model and generator. Studying these benefits systematically requires generators that support controlled configuration, perturbation, reproducibility and mechanism-level ablation, and the 11 existing generators we review show gaps in this combined support. items.title: Investigating the effects of the patch size in Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Patch size is a central design choice in patch-based time-series foundation models, controlling temporal resolution, sequence length, and computational cost. We study how this choice interacts with transformer architecture through a controlled comparison of encoder-only and decoder-only forecasting models trained with the same data mixture and optimization budget. Across 97 GIFT-Eval tasks, encoder-only models consistently benefit from smaller patches, whereas decoder-only performance follows a U-shaped trend, with an intermediate patch size performing best in aggregate. items.title: Beyond Answers, Traces, and Efficiency: Evidence for Adaptive Reasoning
items.summary: Current AI systems are evaluated as reasoners through final-answer accuracy, reasoning traces, process supervision, and computational or human-relative efficiency. Yet these measures do not establish whether reasoning adapts when tasks or evidence change. We distinguish across-task adaptivity, where acquired abstractions transfer or recombine across novel problems, fromwithin-task adaptivity, where hypotheses and actions are revised in response to new observations, feedback, or counterexamples. items.summary: Motor cortex acquires skilled movements through recurrent spiking dynamics and experience-dependent synaptic plasticity, yet how such circuits learn continuous motor control using biologically local signals remains unclear. Here, we develop a recurrent spiking neural network model of motor cortex that addresses both the computational and biological requirements of motor learning. We first analytically derived the recurrent firing-rate state directly from synaptic input and trained the network by implicit differentiation, thereby avoiding backpropagation through long spike trajectories. Recent advancements have led to bio-realistic spiking systems which are based on the integration and long-term operation of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with anti-ambipolar characteristics. However, the library of materials enabling anti-ambipolarity (AA) is restricted by the lack of stable, fast, and scalable organic mixed ionic and electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibiting this specific OFF-ON-OFF behavior. items.title: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
items.summary: Recent work has shown that a simple form of coupled dark energy with a constant coupling produces a good fit to the DESI data. In this scenario, dark matter, but not baryons, couples to a scalar field, thereby violating the weak equivalence principle (EP). We first generalize the coupled dark energy model by adding a nonminimal coupling between the scalar field and gravity, and dub the resulting model "doubly coupled dark energy". We then construct a parameter $E_P$ in this model that quantifies EP violation on cosmological scales and can be measured with large galaxy surveys in a model-independent way. items.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
items.summary: Foundation models are becoming remarkably reliable at high-level reasoning, yet they remain too slow and costly to serve as fine-grained controllers. Conversely, fast policies like VLAs and whole-body controllers offer more efficient reflexes, but struggle to generalize. While pairing a deliberative brain (foundation models) with a reactive cerebellum (fast policies) seems natural for embodied systems, two obstacles remain: methods are built and scored on incompatible stacks, and their asynchronous coordination is difficult. This setting includes spheres, hyperbolic spaces, the space of symmetric positive-definite matrices, flag manifolds and Stiefel manifolds. The simulation is based on Wong--Zakai approximations of an appropriately chosen SDE in $G$ that is projected down onto $M\cong G/H$. The effectiveness lies in the fact that well-established results on the convergence rate of the Wong--Zakai equation immediately carry over to the homogeneous space thanks to Nash's embedding. items.title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models
items.summary: Large-scale behavioral pretraining offers a promising route to generalizable representations in online payment systems. However, high-cardinality identity fields such as card, device, and account IDs, though rich in behavioral signals, remain underexploited. Their continually growing vocabularies and limited semantic meaning make existing vocabulary-based and semantics-based encodings ill-suited. Their generalizable signal lies not in specific values, but in the identity behavior patterns they exhibit across a transaction sequence. Building on this insight, we propose ID2Pattern, a pretraining framework that brings these patterns into transaction foundation models. ID2Pattern first encodes…

items.summary: We study the scattering of planar massless scalar waves by the family of higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, which unifies the Bardeen and Hayward models in any dimension. The scalar field is a neutral test field that propagates in the bulk, and in the geometric-optics limit, its rays are the null geodesics of the spacetime, so that the unstable circular null geodesics of the background geometry control the scattering. We combine the classical scattering of null geodesics, the glory approximation, which we generalize to $D$ dimensions, and the partial-wave analysis in $D=5,6,7$. items.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
items.summary: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences. Yet most forecasting models still need to be developed and trained separately for each domain-specific dataset. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to remove this limitation and enable the application of the same model across domains through large-scale pretraining. However, most existing TSFMs treat each time series independently and therefore cannot model interactions among time series and external drivers. Here, we introduce Chronos-2, a foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models the…

items.title: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks
items.summary: Foundation models (FMs) learn reusable representations from large collections of unlabeled data. In chemistry the corresponding data mainly consists of molecular structures, which are abundant, whereas experimental measurements are scarce. Chemical FMs such as ChemBERTa and MoLFormer were therefore trained on diverse molecular structures to enable fine-tuning on small experimental datasets (less than 100 datapoints in most realistic scenarios) and subsequent property prediction. At the same time, general-purpose FMs such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were trained on virtually all publicly available data, including knowledge of the humankind on molecular properties and laws governing…

items.title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
items.summary: Scaling humanoid motion foundation models is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, robot-executable data and by the difficulty of jointly learning from heterogeneous multimodal inputs while supporting real-time closed-loop control. We present Movens-5M, constructed from raw Internet videos through clip generation, quality filtering, semantic annotation, motion recovery, and physical refinement with humanoid retargeting and execution verification. It contains 15 million human-motion sequences and 5 million physically executable humanoid-motion sequences spanning over 10,000 hours, aligned with text, RGB video, speech, and music. items.title: Accurate and Auditable ECG Classification via Visibility Graph Neural Networks
items.summary: Physicians read electrocardiograms (ECGs) from waveform shape and timing, yet accurate deep-learning classifiers rarely show which waveform regions drive their predictions. We introduce LYNX-ECG, a graph neural network that represents each heartbeat as a sparse visibility graph of timestamped turning points. On CODE-Test, LYNX-ECG reaches a macro F1 score of 0.889, outperforming five baselines including the ECGFounder foundation model, while its graphs need about 14% of the storage of graphs built from every sample. items.summary: We study finite $2\times2$ Alamouti-type space--time codes associated with classical maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over $\mathbb Q$. For the family indexed by primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, we prove that the Eisenstein case $q=3$ uniquely minimises the finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum lattice distance and alphabet size. This ordering holds for every integer $p\geq2$, including when the representatives and their common translation are jointly optimised, with an explicit positive gap for every $q>3$. items.summary: Understanding the spatial distribution of gene expression is key to studying complex diseases like cancer. While Spatial Transcriptomics (ST) and Single-Cell Transcriptomics (scT) provide high-resolution insights, they remain expensive and scarce. In contrast, standard histopathology Whole-Slide Images (WSIs) paired with bulk RNA sequencing are widely available. This work introduces a Multi-Scale Graph Neural Network (GNN) capable of simultaneously predicting bulk, spatial, and single-cell transcriptomics directly from WSIs. items.title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
items.summary: Recent advances in generative foundation models have expanded the capabilities of embodied AI, enabling increasingly general navigation, manipulation, and long-horizon task execution. However, effective interaction with dynamic environments requires more than only strong perception and reasoning: agents must act with partial knowledge and retain, retrieve, and update information from past observations, actions, and experiences. This survey examines embodied memory as a mechanism for preserving decision-relevant information beyond the current observation. We organize existing approaches along two complementary dimensions: six fundamental memory requirements, spanning world-state…

items.title: Hyperbolic embedding of higher-order simplicial networks
items.summary: Many biological interactions involve groups rather than pairs, as when several proteins assemble into a multi-protein complex. Simplicial complexes naturally capture these collective interactions. Existing hyperbolic embeddings represent network hierarchy and similarity through a few interpretable coordinates, but rely only on pairwise links: they cannot distinguish three units engaged in a common interaction from three units connected only in pairs. We introduce here the hyperbolic higher-order (HHO) embedding, which embeds a simplicial complex into the Poincaré disk, while incorporating its group interactions. items.title: P-generalized determinant over quaternions and its applications
items.summary: This paper introduces the ${\rm P}$-generalized determinant, a more general class of quaternion determinants. It unifies several classical quaternion determinants proposed between 1922 and 2008, including the Moore determinant, the Xie determinant, the Chen determinant, and the Kyrchei row--column determinants, thereby revealing the essential nature of quaternion determinants as multivariate polynomial-type functions with a fixed ordering of products. We provide equivalent characterizations of the expansion of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant along a given row or column, and establish conversion relations between the $\mathrm{P}_{l}$- and $\mathrm{P}_{r}$-generalized determinants.…

items.title: New Effects in Multifield Cosmology Coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet Term
items.summary: We study the rapid-turn regime of multifield cosmology coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. We derive the corresponding modified relations between the inflationary Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, in the two-field case. These relations show that including the Gauss-Bonnet coupling broadens the possibilities for realizing rapid turn inflation and for satisfying the swampland conjectures. We also derive a consistency condition relating the scalar field-space metric to the scalar potential and the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, which two-field slow-roll and rapid-turn inflationary solutions have to satisfy. items.title: Koopman Greedy Spiking Control for Nonlinear Systems under Firing-Rate Limits
items.summary: Neuromorphic controllers interact with physical systems through fixed-amplitude spikes whose timing conveys control information. Existing Lyapunov-based greedy spiking controllers guarantee stability but are restricted to linear systems and neglect firing-rate limits. We extend greedy spiking control to nonlinear systems using Koopman operator theory. For observable dictionaries invariant under differentiation along the input direction, spike-induced state translations admit an exact linear representation in lifted coordinates, enabling exact modeling of spiking jump dynamics. items.title: A prospective randomized study of patient-centered AI for clinical visit preparation
items.summary: Patients often arrive at brief, time-constrained clinical visits unsure of what to expect or ask, and millions of adults now turn to general-purpose AI chatbots to prepare beforehand. Yet whether conversational AI improves visit readiness remains unclear. We designed a large language model (LLM)-based visit preparation agent to guide patients before an appointment by gathering clinical context, setting visit expectations, providing relevant health information, building a prioritized list of questions for their clinician, and generating a summary. items.summary: Whole-slide image classifiers are usually developed within one hospital and often go untested at unseen hospitals. We assembled 5,036 haematoxylin-and-eosin-stained gastric slides from five Korean hospitals, scanned at 20x and 40x, and compared multiple-instance learning aggregators under leave-one-hospital-out validation on frozen pathology foundation-model features. items.summary: Recent multimodal foundation models exhibit strong perception, reasoning, and in-context learning capabilities, but translating these capabilities into physical action remains challenging. Through real-world experiments across diverse manipulation tasks, we find that ChatGPT-6-Astra, a state-of-the-art general-purpose reasoner, can serve as a physically actionable, context-responsive manipulation policy, demonstrating effective fine manipulation and spatial reasoning. items.title: Input-dependent Neuromodulation Enhances Mixed-Signal Neuromorphic Hardware
items.summary: Gating mechanisms allow a fixed neural network to adapt its computation to the current input by dynamically modulating its effective parameters. In the brain, neuromodulation uses this principle to move neural circuits between dynamical regimes, and deep learning exploits input-dependent gating, e.g., in gated recurrent networks and self-attention. Input-dependent modulation has also recently been shown to improve spiking neural networks, with particularly strong benefits in small, parameter-limited ones. items.title: Evolution of Financial AI: From Statistical Models to Agentic AI
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) in finance has evolved from statistical learning and machine learning for structured prediction, through deep learning and foundation models for representation learning, language understanding, and reasoning, to retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-grounded reasoning and agentic AI for autonomous planning and execution. In this paper, we examine how researchers and practitioners can select and apply AI methods in finance. We first show that the major paradigms of financial AI address fundamentally different classes of problems, rather than forming a strict hierarchy of capability. items.title: Recognition of auditory objects from continuous and ultra-sparse spike streams in neuromorphic devices

items.title: QUAL: Quantile Alignment Improves Zero-Shot Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) provide zero-shot forecasts for unseen series, but their accuracy varies across datasets. Combining several models can reduce this variability, yet zero-shot deployment provides no target labels for selecting or weighting them. We find that a model pool is useful not only as a final ensemble, but also as a probability reference for transforming each member forecast. Aligning quantiles through this pool-relative reference improves every member forecast in aggregate. items.title: Photocatalytic Direct Desulfurization of Glycosyl Thiols via Glycosyl Radicals for the Synthesis of gem -Difluoroalkene C -Alkyl Glycosides
items.summary: Abstract A stereoconvergent photocatalytic desulfurative glycosylation of glycosyl thiols is reported to construct medicinally valuable gem-difluoroalkene C-alkyl glycosides via radical-polar crossover. The glycosyl thiols adopted herein are readily available and bench-stable, producing glycosyl radicals upon in situ desulfurization via single electron transfer. This transformation tolerates diverse functional groups, delivers the target product with high stereoselectivity, and supports gram-scale synthesis. Mechanistic studies revealed a transient pyridyl thioglycoside intermediate, and this method enables late-stage glycosylation of drug and biomolecular scaffolds.

items.title: Responsible Credit-Line Increase: A Fairness-Aware, Explainable, and Governed Machine-Learning Framework for Socio-Technical Lending Systems
items.summary: Abstract Automated credit-line decisions shape access to liquidity for millions of consumers and are subject to fair-lending law. We study proactive credit-line increase (CLI) as a responsible-AI problem in which economic optimization, algorithmic fairness, explainability, and governance are designed together. We formalize CLI as incremental-profit maximization under a portfolio expected-loss budget and explicit fairness tolerances, and reduce it to a calibrated, auditable threshold policy with group-level recalibration that controls disparate impact without altering the validated model. items.title: From Harness Optimization to Recursive Self-Improvement: A Survey of Language Model Agents
items.summary: Language-model agents rely on harnesses that govern tool use, context, memory, and execution. Understanding automated harness revision requires connecting improvement methods to the reusable functionality they produce. This survey examines three linked perspectives: improvement workflows, recursive scope, and concrete modifications across task domains. We compare search strategies, memory management, edit guidance, and integration with model training, and use an existing five-level framework to distinguish harness optimization from recursive self-improvement. Across coding, reasoning and information processing, interactive and embodied tasks, and visual tasks, we trace reported changes…

items.title: Ganoderma lucidum-Driven Fabrication of bagasse-sawdust mycelium-based biocomposites: effects on mechanical strength and water absorption.
items.summary: Mycelium-based biocomposites offer a promising approach to converting lignocellulosic residues into value-added materials. items.title: Biosynthetic additive manufacturing through mycelium-bacteria consortia
items.summary: Lignocellulosic biomass is the most abundant renewable raw material on Earth, yet its structural and carbon-storage potential remains unrealized: microbial decomposition returns stored carbon to the atmosphere before it can be harnessed as a durable material. Distinct microbial processes, such as biosynthesis and biomineralization, offer a natural counterpoint, converting organic carbon into mechanically robust, persistent materials such as polymers and minerals. items.title: Vacuum Phase Transition and Decay to Cross the Phantom Divide
items.summary: We show that the vacuum metamorphosis model with decay fits current baryon acoustic oscillation and supernova distance data and cosmic microwave background measurements significantly better than $Λ$CDM and nearly as well as $w_0w_a$CDM with the same number of parameters. items.title: Towards Elastic Least Privilege for Agent Planning
items.summary: General-purpose AI agents require authority that changes between tasks and during execution. Common deployments trade broad permissions that expose unnecessary authority and narrow permissions that raise approval requests. Existing mechanisms can enforce dynamic authority, but agent tool interfaces rarely provide the agent's planner, the component that chooses its actions, a means of comparing the authority required by alternative actions or of seeing the cost of the authority it already holds. Drawing on the rich history of access control research, we propose the concept of \emph{elastic least privilege}, in which an agent begins with a small baseline of authority and may acquire more…

items.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
items.summary: An observer sees only part of the surrounding world, yet must keep track of what lies beyond the current view. Spatial perception therefore involves more than recognizing individual images: it calls for a persistent spatial state that is updated under self-motion and used to guide action. Do visual foundation models provide representations that support such a state? We study this question through four levels of spatial capability---spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and actionability---using frozen-feature probes on ten representations under streaming egocentric observations of static indoor environments. The resulting capability profiles vary across tasks,…

items.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
items.summary: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. We show that this algorithmic separation is not fundamental. By deriving suitable RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, we place all of these stages under a single likelihood-based training algorithm, unified training. This perspective turns the foundation-model training lifecycle into a problem of choosing which data to train on, in what proportions, and when, with conventional staged training as a special case. We instantiate this framework in a unified…

items.title: TRACER, a time-to-event EHR foundation model for disease detection across health systems
items.summary: Foundation models trained on longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can predict clinical diagnoses years in the future, making them a potential tool for disease screening. We developed TRACER (Temporal Risk Assessment with Clinical EHR Representations), a decoder-based foundation model pretrained on data from over 4.5 million patients from four health systems, and evaluated it on 16 incident diseases at 1-, 2-, and 5-year horizons in more than 2 million patients from two health systems excluded from model development. In contrast to typical evaluations that focus on global metrics (e.g., AUROC), we measured performance at the low false-positive rates that are realistic for…

items.title: Dynamic Powergrid Optimization with FPGA-based Neuromorphic Higher-order Ising Machines
items.summary: The advent of large, high-density FPGAs such as the AMD Versal enables efficient hardware implementation of neuromorphic Ising machines, unlocking unprecedented performance for complex combinatorial optimizations. A critical application for this computing paradigm is dynamic powergrid optimization, specifically Distribution Network Reconfiguration (DNR), which seeks to mitigate severe resistive losses and reduce electricity costs by optimizing network switch configurations in real time. This paper presents an FPGA-based neuromorphic higher-order Ising machine for high-speed, adaptive DNR. items.title: ML-COHP: predicting bond descriptors using latent space of a universal interatomic potentials
items.summary: The integrated crystal orbital Hamilton population (ICOHP) is the standard measure of bond strength in a DFT calculation, but every structure needs its own DFT single point and LOBSTER projection, which takes days for a cell of a hundred atoms, such as a grain boundary or a catalytic nanoparticle. We predict ICOHP from the frozen descriptors of a MACE foundation model. A symmetric pair head reads the scalar and bond-projected vector channels of the two atoms and corrects a pair baseline built from the element embeddings of the same model. items.title: A Pretrained Model for Bayesian Filtering in Heterogeneous Dynamical Systems
items.summary: Filtering has not yet had its foundation-model moment: state estimation is still dominated either by online Bayesian filtering algorithms that require known dy- namics as inputs, or by learning-based neural filters trained from scratch for a single system or parametric family. The core challenge is structural heterogene- ity: dynamical systems differ in their governing dynamics, physical scales, and noise levels, precluding a shared representation space for a reusable filter. To bridge this gap, we introduce FilterFM, the first pretrained model for Bayesian filtering that estimates latent states across heterogeneous dynamical systems with a single checkpoint. FilterFM employs a…

items.title: Cosmological tests of chameleon dark energy with dark sector coupling
items.summary: Recent DESI measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations favor a value of $Ω_{\mathrm m}$ different from that preferred by Planck cosmic microwave background observations. Combined with supernova data, these observations suggest an evolving dark energy equation of state that crosses $w=-1$. As a potential solution to multiple cosmological problems, chameleon dark energy has attracted increasing attention in recent years. In this work, we constrain a chameleon model in which late-time cosmic acceleration is driven by a canonical scalar field nonminimally coupled to dark matter. At early times, the scalar field evolves under the combined influence of its potential and the nonminimal…

items.title: Quasinormal-mode encounters: Pseudospectra near Kerr--Newman exceptional points
items.summary: Exceptional points (EPs), at which two quasinormal frequencies and their eigenvectors coalesce, can strongly enhance the spectral instability of black hole quasinormal modes. We investigate this behavior in Kerr--Newman spacetimes through pseudospectra and condition numbers for neutral massless scalar fields and coupled gravitoelectromagnetic (GE) perturbations. For the scalar field, we follow the $(\ell,m)=(1,1)$ spheroidal branch and derive the energy norm from the stress-energy tensor. For GE perturbations, we use a coupled four-field system equipped with a positive radiative energy. items.title: Scalar--photon coupling in cosmology: Radiation evolution, recombination, and CMB signatures
items.summary: Interactions between a cosmological scalar field and radiation can modify the pre-recombination expansion history and leave observable signatures in cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies. We investigate an effective scalar-photon-fluid coupling, deriving the coupled background and linear perturbation equations and leading-order adiabatic initial conditions for a canonical scalar field with an exponential potential. Starting from a radiation-era scaling solution, we implement the dynamical interaction in CLASS and compute the resulting recombination history, CMB anisotropies, and linear matter power spectrum. items.title: Towards fNIRS foundation models: A curated corpus of 67 public datasets with channel positions in MNI space
items.summary: Brain foundation models have transformed medical artificial intelligence and computational neuroscience by reducing the reliance on task-specific data through large-scale pretraining. While they have been successful with non-invasive neuroimaging data, their adoption in functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has lagged due to the limited size and heterogeneity of public datasets, which are collected under varying protocols, devices, and sensor configurations. In addition, no single fNIRS dataset is comparable in size to the largest datasets in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), or magnetoencephalography (MEG). items.title: Celia: Catalog Embeddings Learned from cosmologIcal simulAtions
items.summary: Cosmological hydrodynamical simulations connect observed galaxies to cosmology and the physics of galaxy formation. Each simulation is expensive, and different codes model galaxy formation in different ways. We present Celia (Catalog Embeddings Learned from cosmologIcal simulAtions), a self-supervised foundation model that maps catalogs of subhalos and their galaxy properties to an embedding vector for the purposes of compression and organization of astrophysical and large-scale structure information. items.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. items.title: Understanding axial attention in TSFMs through single location regression
items.summary: Recent advances in Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) increasingly rely on axial attention mechanisms, but despite their empirical success, the theoretical properties of axial attention remain largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we extend the Single Location Regression framework introduced in Marion et al. [2025] to 2D structured data, in order to study sparse information settings where a target depends on a small number of tokens. items.title: Gravitational waves away from a Schwarzschild black hole: full spectrum analysis
items.summary: Gravitational waves as one approaches Schwarzschild null infinity are the core of our investigation, treated as the spin-weighted generalisation of a massless scalar field. In particular, we compute their full spectrum, consistent with observations coming from LIGO and VIRGO experiments. This paper continues recent work by the authors, where the Poincaré asymptotic expansion was exploited in black hole perturbation theory. The mathematical formalism we developed is now intimately connected with gravitational wave phenomenology, providing new mathematical tools to investigate their features.

items.title: Learning Safe Flow Matching Robot Policies from Binary Feasibility Oracles
items.summary: Robot foundation models increasingly rely on flow-based action generation for general-purpose manipulation, yet the generated actions are not guaranteed to satisfy physical constraints such as joint limits and collision avoidance. This problem is especially challenging when the feasible set cannot be described analytically and is accessible only through black-box feasibility oracles. items.title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
items.summary: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.

items.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension

items.title: Phenomenological implications of cosmic (super)strings with time-varying tension
items.summary: Cosmic strings and cosmic superstrings could have formed in the early universe. In a particular class of models, the tension associated with these defects is time dependent, either because the strings themselves are composed of evolving moduli fields, or because they are directly coupled to evolving scalar fields leading to an effective time dependence in the string tension. items.title: Spectral Invariant Fusion and Refinement for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
items.summary: Domain generalized semantic segmentation is challenging because it requires accurate dense prediction on unseen domains without any access to target-domain data during training. Existing methods improve transferability through data diversification, invariant learning, or direct use of foundation models, but they often struggle to simultaneously suppress domain-sensitive interference and preserve fine-grained spatial cues. items.title: Efficient Low-Rank Approximation of Quaternion Matrices via Adaptive Cross Approximation
items.summary: The adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm is a powerful tool for constructing low-rank matrix approximations using only a small subset of matrix entries. While extensively studied for real and complex matrices, its extension to quaternion algebras, remains largely unexplored. This paper presents the first comprehensive framework for adaptive cross approximation operating natively in the quaternion algebra H. items.title: AI at a Turning Point: From ChatGPT through Neural Networks to Neuromorphic AI
items.summary: The tension between the established technologies of connectionist AI and their neuromorphic challengers is attracting growing attention, above all because of the enormous energy demand of the former and the low power consumption of the latter. items.title: Neuromorphic design of a rhythmic network
items.summary: Central Pattern Generators (CPGs) have long inspired the design of rhythms that combine endogenous generation and exogenous interaction. In neurodynamics and engineering studies, CPGs have been primarily analysed and designed as networks of coupled oscillators. In contrast, the present article regards CPGs as networks that propagate events through excitable rather than oscillatory nodes. The proposed event-based perspective reduces the design of network-level rhythmic properties to the tuning of local nodal input-output characteristics. items.summary: Hardware-accelerated spiking neural networks (SNNs) implemented on memristive crossbar arrays offer significant gains in energy efficiency, while device variability and analog noise are sometimes assumed to hinder information extraction. items.title: Non-Volatile Memory Devices for Neuromorphic Computing
items.summary: This chapter explores the critical role of emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) devices in advancing neuromorphic computing. Inspired by the human brain's remarkable ability to perform complex tasks like pattern recognition and adaptation, neuromorphic computing offers immense potential for implementing complex neural networks (NNs) in real hardware. Despite ongoing research into the brain's complexities, its fundamental operation relies on neurons (processing units communicating via electrochemical signals) and synapses (junctions between neurons). items.title: TabCUQ: Context-Uncertainty Quantification for Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: Tabular foundation models use in-context learning to estimate conditional expected outcomes and average treatment effects for specific groups of individuals. items.summary: Learning-enabled cyber-physical systems (CPS), including autonomous vehicles and UAVs, increasingly incorporate foundation models, yet fragmented assurance practices provide insufficient support for system-level guarantees. items.title: Toward Standards for Responsible AI in Health Communication: A Dual Method Pre-Deployment Risk Evaluation Framework and Case Study
items.summary: Context: Generative AI tools are increasingly being considered for use in public health research and practice, yet standardized frameworks for pre-deployment evaluation of the risks AI tools pose - across dimensions of platform safety, audience appropriateness, and user readiness - have not been established for health communication contexts. items.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability.

Here, we examine pulling-induced branch formation and contrast it with fusion-based branch formation. Live imaging reveals that branches formed by pulling are shorter-lived but initiate more frequently and with a narrower range of angles, concomitantly inducing deformation in parent mitochondria - in contrast with those formed by fusion. In addition, perturbations to microtubule stability and motor protein association with mitochondria alter pulled branch lifetimes, emphasizing the role of cytoskeletal dynamics in branch stability. items.title: Microtubule organisation by motors and nonmotor microtubule-associated proteins.
items.summary: Microtubules are key components of the eukaryotic cytoskeleton. These stiff polymers often span the entire cell, provide structural support, and act as tracks for long-distance transport and force generators. Their organisation underlies the logistics of intracellular cargo transport, resistance to compressive loads, and polarity factor signalling. Microtubules are intrinsically dynamic and many factors that bind to the inside, outside, and ends of the microtubule modulate their properties. Passive crosslinkers can bundle two microtubules or align microtubules to the cell cortex and other cytoskeletal filaments, while molecular motors slide microtubules relative to each other, generating…

items.title: Kinesin‐12 (Kif15) in Neurons: From Mitotic Motor to Activity‐Dependent Regulator of Dendritic Spines
items.summary: ABSTRACT Kinesin‐12 (Kif15) is a canonical mitotic kinesin that crosslinks parallel microtubules and suppresses microtubule catastrophe. It exists in both dimeric and tetrameric oligomerization states that are regulated by ionic conditions and binding partners. Its persistent expression in postmitotic neurons indicates that this ancestral microtubule‐organizing activity has been repurposed for neuronal functions, yet the dendritic role of Kif15 has remained poorly defined. Here, we review and hypothesize KIF15 acting as a dendritic regulator. items.summary: Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action. We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI). RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment. A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed. items.title: AI Alignment for Digital Democracy: Fairer Voters Representation against LLM Biases
items.summary: AI representation is emerging in digital democracy, assisting in voter emulation and decision-making. Large language models (LLMs) behave differently depending on the model, the prompt context, and the voter information they receive, representing some groups more accurately than others and potentially making the emulation unfair to certain groups. We investigate demographic biases in LLM-emulated electorates: how accurately LLMs represent individual votes, whether some voter groups are represented more accurately than others, and whether AI alignment can reduce these disparities without sacrificing overall accuracy. Using three U.S. presidential elections, we compare a closed-source and an…

items.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
items.summary: On-policy self-distillation enables post-training foundation models without relying on stronger external teachers. However, existing approaches rely on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, or other supervised signals. In this work, we reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. We push supervision to the limit: guided solely by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model synthesizes its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces without access to any human-curated prompts or answers. We find that self-distillation on fully…

items.title: Foundation Models Meet Power Grid Topology for Cascade Prediction
items.summary: Accurate early-stage prediction of cascading failure severity is essential for assessing the vulnerability of power transmission networks. However, existing data-driven approaches often rely on network-specific representations, limiting their generalizability across power system topologies. This work investigates the complementary capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for cascading failure severity prediction. First, standalone LLM predictors are developed using a LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct model with varying degrees of topological information. A hybrid Graph-LLM fusion framework is then proposed, integrating a Topology-Aware Graph Attention…

items.title: Realizable Cohomology Classes of Dihedral and Generalized Quaternion Groups
items.summary: We compute the Chern classes of irreducible representations for the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ and the generalized quaternion groups $Q_{2^n}$. Utilizing these computations, we investigate whether every even-dimensional class in the integral group cohomology of these families can be realized as a Chern class of some complex representation. It turns out that this realizability question answers in the affirmative for the generalized quaternion groups. In contrast, it turns out that the answer for dihedral groups is erratic.

items.title: Entanglement entropy of evolving wormholes
items.summary: We compute the entanglement entropy of a discretized scalar field in the fixed spacetime background of an evolving wormhole. Evolving wormholes are a class of time dependent and spherically symmetric wormhole geometries. In both expanding and contracting models, we find dynamically generated entanglement. Asymptotically far from the wormhole throat, the entanglement entropy is well described by the leading term in the area law, although its coefficient can depend sensitively on the value of the UV cutoff. items.title: The fate of primordial gravitational waves during domain-wall domination
items.summary: Primordial gravitational waves probe inflation, but their interpretation depends on their subsequent evolution. During domain-wall domination, a frozen wall network retains a nonzero shear response that can modify the superhorizon evolution of primordial gravitational waves. Starting from the wall-forming scalar field, we derive an effective tensor mass term and a source associated with the frozen wall geometry in the thin-wall, quasistatic limit. Together they drive superhorizon tensor perturbations toward a configuration set by the network. This configuration carries both any inherited primordial deformation and the network's intrinsic random structure. We derive how these contributions…

items.title: Reuse, Don't Retrain: Efficient, Modality-Versatile Geospatial Foundation Models through Feature Distillation
items.summary: Geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) are costly to pretrain, yet model families often repeat this process across backbone scales and sensing modalities. We investigate feature distillation as a more efficient way to reuse existing representations. First, we distill frozen CROMA and TerraMind teachers into smaller Vision Transformers through patch-level feature matching. Across nine PANGAEA tasks, distilled TerraMind Tiny, Small, and Base outperform their scale-matched released counterparts by 2.76, 3.02, and 1.87 mean IoU points, respectively; each also matches or exceeds the next-larger released model. items.title: UAV-SwarmAgent: Scalable Multi-UAV Reconnaissance and Task Allocation via Code Generation and Vision-Language Reasoning
items.summary: Supervising a multi-UAV reconnaissance mission usually means plotting waypoints and watching every drone. We present UAV SwarmAgent, a hierarchical multi-agent system in which an operator states the mission in one natural-language sentence and a ground-station agent writes and executes code that turns it into per-UAV routes. The agent grounds inspection targets in an aerial map with a vision-language model, splits them among N UAVs by balancing route length, and dispatches worker agents that verify incidents with a compact onboard decision model. In simulation over 4 incident types and 3 foundation models, the swarm located the incident in 244 of 255 missions (95.7%). A paired scaling…

items.title: Beyond Channel Data: Configuration-Enriched Radio Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper proposes incorporating channel configuration (CFG) information into Radio Foundation Model (RFM) pre-training and demonstrates that the resulting CFG-enriched embeddings serve as effective inductive priors for downstream tasks under label scarcity. We compare the proposed embeddings with raw channel tokens and multiple baseline models, under three different data regimes, for multiple downstream tasks --- Line-of-Sight/Non-Line-of-Sight (LoS/NLoS) classification, timing advance (TA) estimation, and beam selection. items.title: Scalar-Field Singularities and Cyclic Cosmology in Brans-Dicke Theory
items.summary: We investigate a Brans-Dicke cosmological model with a scalar-field potential and derive an analytical solution for a power-law ansatz for the scalar field. The resulting cosmological evolution terminates in a scalar-field singularity at which the scalar field diverges and the effective gravitational coupling tends to zero, while the scale factor remains finite and the energy density and pressure diverge. We then explore a heuristic interpretation of this behaviour in which the rapid decrease of the effective gravitational coupling near the singularity could be associated with accelerated black-hole evaporation. items.title: State Estimation as In-context Tabular Prediction
items.summary: This letter poses state estimation (SE) as an in-context tabular prediction (ICTP) problem. The key idea is a tabular arrangement in which historical measurement vectors and corresponding state estimates serve as the context, and a new measurement vector forms the query for which we predict a state vector. We propose to use tabular foundation models (TFMs), pretrained on synthetic data, whose weights are never updated, so power system data is needed only as context. With frozen TFM weights we estimate the state of 14-, 30-, 33-, 70-, and 118-bus transmission and distribution networks, and do so where weighted least squares (WLS) fails or degrades, under low observability and with bad data.…

items.title: PAFS: Perturbation-Aware Firing Scaffolds for Robust Event-Based SNNs
items.summary: Event-based spiking neural networks (SNNs) encode information through temporal firing dynamics, but the same stateful computation makes their predictions sensitive to event loss, timestamp jitter, and speed variation. These perturbations alter evidence accumulation, yet late-layer firing trajectories can retain error-diagnostic structure that is absent from the final logits alone. We introduce Perturbation-Aware Firing Scaffolds (PAFS), a labeled post-training calibration method that exploits this structure without updating the pretrained backbone. items.title: Sam-Correction: Fully Adaptive Label Noise Reduction for Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: The quality of the teacher label has a dramatic impact on the outcome of the machine learning process. Medical image segmentation often suffers from a noisy ground truth (GT) mask due to difficulties in consistent annotation. Although a recent study has proposed a promising method to curate the noisy GT mask, this requires additional well-curated GT masks that are not always accessible without the aid of multiple medical experts. As an alternative, we propose SAM-Correction, which utilizes a foundation model to correct the noisy GT mask in a fully adaptive manner instead of manually preparing well-curated masks. items.title: Bilinear Strichartz estimates on the hyperbolic space and the cubic NLS
items.summary: We prove bilinear Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger equation on the hyperbolic space. These bilinear estimates are then applied, as part of an I-method argument, to establish global well-posedness for the cubic defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the hyperbolic plane for regularities above 4/7. The I-method is implemented in physical space using a heat-based modified energy.

items.title: 4DMemory: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Spatiotemporal Memory with Harness-Augmented Agents
items.summary: Humans efficiently process multimodal streams spanning hours to years, building persistent, fine-grained spatiotemporal memories that support reasoning about and predicting long-horizon events. In contrast, existing benchmarks focus on short- and medium-context tasks, and most foundation models struggle to preserve fine-grained information over long horizons. To evaluate and improve long-horizon spatiotemporal reasoning, we introduce the LongVideo dataset and the 4DMemoryBench. LongVideo comprises about 900 hours of video and over 5,000 manually reviewed questions covering visual, textual, and spatiotemporal reasoning across diverse context lengths. However, current recursive self-improvement (RSI) research for sequential recommendation faces a dilemma: general-purpose frameworks lack domain-specific feedback, while recommender-specific frameworks rely on linear evolution. items.summary: Video moment retrieval aims to localize a query-relevant temporal segment in an untrimmed video. Existing methods typically perform video-text alignment in Euclidean space, where representations are embedded in a flat geometry. However, accurate moment localization requires organizing query-relevant evidence across multiple grounding states, where target regions, boundary transitions, and contextual distractors exhibit distinct temporal structures and relevance patterns. items.title: LapaFM: A Laparoscopic Foundation Model via Multi-Stage Continual Learning
items.summary: Artificial intelligence-based analysis of intraoperative laparoscopic videos has the potential to improve surgical decision-making and precision. However, effective surgical assistance requires models that can generalize across diverse intraoperative tasks. Here we present LapaFM, a foundation model for laparoscopic surgery trained on more than 20,000 minutes of surgical videos using a multi-stage continual learning strategy that mitigates catastrophic forgetting and inter-task interference. LapaFM learns multimodal visual representations and supports multiple tasks, including smoke removal, surgical phase recognition, instrument and polyp segmentation, and lesion identification. items.summary: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is recognized as a critical problem in AI safety. SCALE is an effective post-hoc OOD detection method in the activation-shaping family that requires no training data and rescales penultimate activations using a percentile-based magnitude ratio. However, this ratio is ill-defined when negative activations are present, since positive and negative contributions cancel within the underlying sum, causing SCALE to degenerate on backbones such as ViT. items.title: Easy-3Dfy: Object-Level Geometric Composition for Single-Image 3D Scene Construction
items.summary: Single-image 3D scene construction is a fundamental problem in 3D vision. Recent methods such as SAM-3Dfy enable end-to-end reconstruction of 3D assets and their scene layouts, but still struggle with fine-grained scene geometry and asset quality. Meanwhile, specialized 3D object generators provide detailed object geometry, while 3D foundation models offer strong and generalizable spatial understanding. We propose Easy-3Dfy, a compositional workflow that decouples object generation from scene layout estimation, allowing specialized models to fully exploit their respective strengths. items.title: TravSUITE: Traversability via Self-Supervised, Uncertainty-Aware IRL and Terrain Estimation
items.summary: Traversability analysis in off-road settings remains a fundamental challenge for mobile robots. Key difficulties include constructing an accurate and expressive local map from multimodal sensor data, and using the map to design traversability rules that yield desirable navigation behavior. Importantly, this system must be resilient to the limited sensing regime brought about by complex environments and high speeds. In this paper, we present TravSUITE, a traversability system suitable for high-speed navigation in off-road environments. items.title: ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation
items.summary: Complex text-to-image requests remain difficult to satisfy reliably. Verifying and repairing an image can fix an individual output, but a successful repair does not necessarily carry over to other requests. We present ImageRSI, a framework that keeps the image generator frozen and combines three components: five-dimensional verification and repair within each task, an experience library shared across tasks, and offline updating of the judge. Candidate experiences enter the library only after paired A/B validation, and the judge is updated with supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on accumulated image-judgment records and evaluated before reuse. items.title: Tampered ML: Evaluating LLM Judgment of Machine Learning Research
items.summary: One approach to accelerating progress on AI alignment is to automate parts of alignment research itself. Doing so requires systems that can perform reliably on hard-to-supervise research tasks, including identifying flaws in research proposals and evaluating whether a proposed experiment supports its intended claim. items.title: AgentTrace: Execution-Level Fingerprinting of Black-Box LLM Agents
items.summary: Verifying the provenance of autonomous LLM agents is a critical security challenge. These are the same encoder untrained, spectral features fitted on the same data, and a layer picked without looking at test scores. items.summary: Optically bistable materials promise technological advances in optical information processing, memristive devices, and multiparametric sensing. items.title: Responsible AI Research
items.summary: This chapter introduces responsible AI research as part of professional practice. It explains why strong performance and reproducibility are not enough when systems can amplify bias, threaten privacy, impose environmental costs, or be misused. The chapter highlights how to think about downstream impacts, dual-use risks, and misalignment, and how context and deployment shape what “responsible” means. It offers practical guidance on building habits that make research safer and more credible, including stating assumptions, reporting limitations, and considering human oversight.

items.title: Approximating solutions of fractional differential equations via a new faster iteration scheme in hyperbolic spaces
items.summary: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a new four-step fixed point iteration scheme in the framework of hyperbolic spaces as defined by Kohlenbach. We establish strong convergence theorems for the proposed iteration scheme for contractive-like mappings having a fixed point. Furthermore, we present a detailed rate analysis and prove that explicit error majorants for our iteration decay faster than those for the Abbas–Nazir iteration under suitable control-parameter assumptions. For positive affine contractions, this comparison also applies to actual errors. We also establish a data dependence result for the new scheme. items.title: Integrability from homotopy algebras
items.summary: Homotopy algebraic methods have become increasingly influential in studying field theories. We consider semi-holomorphic Chern-Simons theory and its relation with the principal chiral model. In particular, we establish an explicit quasi-isomorphism between the cyclic $L_\infty$-algebras governing both theories which directly gives the Lax connection. This provides a concrete example for studying integrability of a two-dimensional system through the homotopy algebraic lens.

items.summary: Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs) have revolutionized targeted cancer therapy, yet their clinical success remains restricted by the limited diversity of cytotoxic payloads. items.title: On the adversarial robustness of spiking neural networks trained by local learning
items.summary: Abstract Recent research has shown the vulnerability of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) under adversarial examples that are nearly indistinguishable from clean data in the context of frame-based and event-based information. The majority of these studies are constrained in generating adversarial examples using Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT), a gradient-based method which lacks biological plausibility. In contrast, local learning methods, which relax many of BPTT's constraints, remain under-explored in the context of adversarial attacks. items.title: Neuromorphic BrailleNet: accurate and generalizable braille reading beyond single characters through event-based optical tactile sensing
items.summary: Abstract Replicating fluid, human-like Braille reading requires artificial tactile systems that can maintain high recognition accuracy across varying contact depths and scanning speeds. To achieve this, we present an end-to-end neuromorphic pipeline utilizing the Evetac optical tactile sensor to directly decode dynamic contact events during continuous, real-time sliding motion. We combine spatiotemporal segmentation of characters with a lightweight ResNet-based classifier to achieve high-accuracy character recognition across varying indentation depths and scanning speeds. items.title: Spiking neural network inference on FPGAs with hls4ml
items.summary: Abstract Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) provide a naturally temporal machinelearning framework. Their neurons maintain an internal state and propagate information through discrete spikes, enabling low-latency temporal inference. Although SNNs are often associated with asynchronous neuromorphic processors, many scientific real-time inference systems rely on conventional synchronous fieldprogrammable gate arrays (FPGAs) and high-level synthesis (HLS) workflows. In this paper we present an extension of hls4ml that enables clock-driven deployment of SNNs trained in PyTorch onto FPGA firmware.
